docs.text: Driver MAX22200 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Analog Devices MAX22200 and MAX22200A octal solenoid and motor drivers. It starts the chip with the datasheet's procedure, switches channels with one 8-bit write (one transfer per switch), programs HIT and HOLD in milliamps or percent, and reads the faults, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes and drives CMD and ENABLE; it does the rest: the programming procedure, the two-phase register access, the unit conversions, the read-back of every register at start-up, and the fault registers of both parts. Octal solenoid and motor driver MAX22200 Analog Devices Function Eight push-pull half-bridges, 200 mΩ, up to 1 A RMS each; HIT then HOLD per channel Regulation Current (CDR, 7-bit, IFS from RREF, low side) or voltage (VDR, PWM duty in 1 % steps) Configurations Low side, high side, parallel pairs, full bridges for latching valves and DC motors Diagnostics OCP, open load, HIT current not reached, plunger movement, overtemperature, UVLO, SPI clock count Interface SPI mode 0, up to 10 MHz; a command byte with CMD high, then 8 or 32 bits; ENABLE, FAULT, TRIGA/TRIGB Supply VM 4.5 V to 36 V; logic inputs 6 V absolute maximum, 1.2 V high What you get ¶ One object per chip. MAX22200<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as Bus , ChannelsActive or DeviceReset . See API guide . Datasheet codes, checked. Config{} holds the reset values of STATUS and every channel; the conversions refuse a current that would round to the unregulated code and a HIT time that would round to "forever". See Drive modes . A fast hot path. Switching is one 8-bit write, one transfer after another switch; a read-back is there per call when you want it. See API guide . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: the bus, CMD and ENABLE and a delay, plus optional FAULT-pin and logging hooks found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Tested without hardware, and honest about it. Host tests and a fuzzer run the driver against a protocol model of the chip; nothing is verified on hardware yet. See Status and limitations . Datasheet ¶ Document Revision Get it Datasheet: MAX22200/MAX22200A 36V, 1A Octal Integrated Serial-Controlled Solenoid and Motor Driver (Analog Devices 19-100531) 1, 2025-03 vendor page Written against these revisions; the SHA-256 of each file is in docs/datasheets.yml . Where each part of the driver is in the datasheet: Datasheet map . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, open a valve in about 20 lines. docs.text: API guide ¶ Every task the driver supports, with the calls that do it. The member list is in the API reference ; what each call promises is on the Contract page. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: ENABLE and the 0.5 ms to SPI ready: Enable Logic Input, p. 14 The HIT and HOLD sequence, and the TRIG and SPI triggers: Functional Description - Two Levels Drive Sequence for Solenoid Valves; Figures 2 and 3, p. 14 High side, parallel pairs and full bridges: Supported Driver Configurations; Tables 6, 7 and 8, p. 20 Overcurrent and open-load protection: Protection Circuits; Overcurrent Protection (OCP); Open-Load Detection (OL), p. 21 Plunger-movement detection, thermal shutdown, UVLO and the HIT check: Detection of Plunger Movement (DPM); Thermal Shutdown (TSD); Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO); HIT Current Not Reached Flag (HHF), p. 22 The programming procedure: Programming Procedure; Figure 6, p. 23 STATUS: Status Register Description (STATUS); Table 10; Register Details, STATUS (0x00), p. 26 FAULT and its two clear-on-read behaviours: Fault Register Description (FAULT); Table 12; Clearing the FAULT Register; Figure 8, p. 28 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ One object per chip: max22200::MAX22200<YourPort> chip(port, config); . The constructor stores the configuration and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the only call that starts the chip. Every other call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized until it has succeeded. Every fallible call returns Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion) before reading value ; on failure value is T{} and error says why. A call sends only what the datasheet needs. Calls that can read back take a trailing Verify verify = Verify::None ; Verify::ReadBack reads the register back and compares it, and its cost is stated per call. The driver keeps a copy of every register it wrote. GetConfig() and GetChannelsOn() cost nothing. Call Transfers With Verify::ReadBack SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() , SetBridge() 1 right after an ONCH write with nothing in between, else 2 3 or 4 SetHoldCode() 2 4 ConfigureChannel() , SetPairMode() , SetFaultMask() , SetDpm() 2 4 ReadStatus() , ReadFaults() , ClearFaults() , ReadChannelConfig() , ReadChannelsOn() 2 EnsureInitialized() 42 (+2 per extra wake-up poll) ApplyConfig() 2 per register that changes Deinitialize() 2 A transfer is one CSB-low period: the command byte, or the 1 or 4 data bytes after it. Start ¶ max22200 :: Error BringUp ( Chip & chip ) { // The one entry point: starts the chip on the first call, then returns Ok with no I/O. After a // failure the next call starts again from the beginning. const auto r = chip . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "MAX22200 init: %s \n " , max22200 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } EnsureInitialized() drives CMD high (its idle level) and ENABLE high, waits tEN (0.5 ms), then runs the programming procedure of Figure 6: it reads STATUS (which clears UVM), then wakes the chip ("wake-up completed?"): a bare ACTIVE = 1 write, tWU (2.5 ms), a STATUS read, repeated every kWakePollUs (10 ms) until ACTIVE reads 1 with UVM clear, for at most Config::wake_timeout_us (100 ms by default). Then it writes STATUS (fault masks, FREQM, pair modes, every channel off, ACTIVE = 1), CFG_CH0 to CFG_CH7 and CFG_DPM. Then it checks what it wrote: STATUS must hold it and every 32-bit write must have echoed its command byte (Figure 10). Next it reads FAULT with every SDI bit high, which clears every flag on both parts: the chip may keep FAULT across an ENABLE cycle (the datasheet does not say ENABLE low clears it), so flags from before the start would hold the FAULT pin and look new. They are reported by GetStartupFaults() . Last, every configuration register read back must equal what was written (CFG_DPM: bits 14:0; bits 31:15 are reserved, some read only with no reset value). COMER is read only and the datasheet does not say what clears it, and a wake write the chip rejected can set it: if it is set when the wake ends, ENABLE goes low for tDIS and high for tEN and STATUS is read again, kStartAttempts times at most (if it stays set, the attempt relies on the read-back and the session reads every switch-off back); a COMER that appears later repeats the procedure, after ENABLE low for tDIS and high again for tEN, up to kStartAttempts times; if every attempt fails, cycle VM. At the wake timeout it returns Undervoltage (UVM still set) or Timeout (UVM clear, ACTIVE still 0), uninitialised, every channel off, ENABLE left high so a retry continues the wake. On any other failure it drives ENABLE low again. It takes 48 transfers when the chip wakes at the first poll, 4 more per extra poll. Error Meaning InvalidArgument The Config fails Validate() ; nothing was sent Bus , Pin The port failed a transfer or a pin write NoDevice SDO read 0xFF throughout: nothing drives it DeviceIdMismatch STATUS read back differs, or a write did not echo its command: SDI, CMD or CSB broken WriteMismatch A configuration register did not take its write Undervoltage UVM still set at Config::wake_timeout_us : VM below UVLO, slow, or UVM stuck (cycle VM) Timeout ACTIVE never read 1 within Config::wake_timeout_us , UVM clear: cycle VM CommunicationError A new COMER in every attempt: the chip miscounts the clocks Switch channels ¶ max22200 :: Error ApplyValveMask ( Chip & chip , uint8_t want , bool safety_critical ) { // Every channel at once: one 8-bit write. ReadBack adds one 8-bit read and a compare; use it // where a lost frame matters more than the two transfers. const auto verify = safety_critical ? max22200 :: Verify :: ReadBack : max22200 :: Verify :: None ; return chip . SetChannelsOn ( want , verify ). error ; } max22200 :: Error OpenOne ( Chip & chip , uint8_t channel ) { // From the driver's copy of ONCH: no STATUS read first (it would clear OVT and UVM). return chip . SetChannel ( channel , true ). error ; } SetChannelsOn(mask) writes ONCH, STATUS[31:24], in one 8-bit write (Programming Procedure, step 5a). SetChannel(channel, on) computes the new mask from the driver's copy and sends the same single write: no STATUS read first. GetChannelsOn() returns the copy. A channel with trigger_pin follows its TRIG pin instead. The Command Register stays in force until it is rewritten (p25), so a switch right after a switch sends only its data byte: 1 transfer . The first switch after anything else sends the command again (2 transfers): after any other register access, a failed transfer or pin write, an ENABLE change ( Deinitialize() , a restart), a COMER in a fault byte, or a Verify::ReadBack (its read changes the command). The data byte's SDO carries STATUS[7:0] (Figure 12), kept in GetLastStatusByte() : watching the fault flags costs nothing. If that byte is 0xFF (no answer: a chip that lost the command in a reset clocks nothing out), the write goes out again with its command, so the command byte shows whether the chip was reset. A miscounted write shows as COMER from the next byte on: the call that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 returns CommunicationError (see What every call checks ); only Verify::ReadBack proves that a given switch landed. With Verify::ReadBack the driver reads ONCH back (8 bits) and compares it: WriteMismatch when the chip did not take it (the copy then takes the value read, and the channels that differ are not trusted for the ChannelsActive check), CommunicationError when the read's fault byte shows COMER (the write had the wrong clock count). The copy changes only when the write went out; after Bus the channels the write would have changed count as on for the ChannelsActive check until a write succeeds. ReadChannelsOn() reads ONCH from the chip without changing the copy. A switch-on in a pair whose mode a failed write left unknown returns Uncertain and sends nothing (see A write whose reply failed ). A switch-off is never refused: in such a pair it switches both channels off, the partner too, because ONCHx = ONCHy = 0 is off in every mode (Tables 6 and 7) and one bit alone could turn a full-bridge Brake into Forward or Reverse. SetBridge(pair, BridgeState::HiZ) does the same. A SetChannelsOn() mask that changes such a pair switches it off; if it asked for a switch-on there, the rest of the mask, every switch-off in it, still goes out, then the call returns Uncertain . The pair goes off rather than keep the copy's bits: after a miscount the copy may show a channel on that the chip has off. A channel that may still be on (a failed write may have switched it on, or no clean fault byte has vouched for its switch-off yet) is always switched off when the mask asks it off, even when the copy already says off. In a full-bridge pair SetChannel(ch, false) sets HiZ (both bits 0, Table 7): the partner goes off too. In a parallel pair both ONCH bits move together; in a full-bridge pair use SetBridge(pair, state) (Table 7): BridgeState OUTx OUTy HiZ Hi-Z Hi-Z Forward VM regulated with CFG_CHy Reverse regulated with CFG_CHx VM Brake ground ground Change a channel's settings ¶ ConfigureChannel(channel, config) writes the whole CFG_CHn (32 bits). Everything but the drive mode and the side can change while the channel runs (step 5c): the currents, the HIT time, the chopping frequency, SRC, the diagnostics. A change of drive mode or side while any channel is on returns ChannelsActive and sends nothing. max22200 :: Error LowerHold ( Chip & chip , uint8_t channel ) { // On the fly, while the channel holds: one 8-bit write of HFS and HOLD. const auto code = max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 150 , chip . GetConfig (). rref_ohm , chip . GetConfig (). channels [ channel ]. half_scale ); if ( ! code ) { return code . error ; // below the resolution or above 126/128 x IFS } return chip . SetHoldCode ( channel , code . value ). error ; } SetHoldCode(channel, code) writes only CFG_CHn[31:24], HFS and HOLD, in one 8-bit write (step 5b), for a HOLD current controlled on the fly; HFS is kept. The code is checked against the channel's drive mode ( ValidCode() ). SetPairMode() , SetFaultMask() and SetDpm() write STATUS or CFG_DPM; a pair mode changes only with both channels of the pair off. ApplyConfig() writes every register of a new Config that differs from the current one. Read and clear faults ¶ void ServiceFaults ( Chip & chip ) { const auto s = chip . ReadStatus (); // clears OVT and UVM if ( ! s ) { if ( s . error == max22200 :: Error :: DeviceReset ) { ( void ) chip . EnsureInitialized (); // power-on reset: configure the chip again } return ; } if ( ! s . value . overcurrent && ! s . value . open_load && ! s . value . hit_not_reached && ! s . value . plunger ) { return ; } const auto f = chip . ClearFaults (); // returns the flags it cleared if ( f && f . value . overcurrent != 0U ) { // OCP switched those channels off: switch them off, then on again when it is safe. const uint32_t on = chip . GetChannelsOn (); const auto keep = static_cast < uint8_t > ( on & ~ static_cast < uint32_t > ( f . value . overcurrent )); ( void ) chip . SetChannelsOn ( keep ); } } ReadStatus() returns ONCH, the seven flags and ACTIVE. The read clears OVT and UVM on the chip (Register Details: "Read Clears All"); the four channel flags (OCP, OLF, HHF, DPM) say only that some channel has one: the FAULT register says which. If ACTIVE reads 0 on a running driver, a power-on reset cleared every register: the driver marks itself uninitialised and returns DeviceReset ; call EnsureInitialized() to configure the chip again. Every other call does the same from its command byte (see What every call checks ). Config::variant is Variant::Max22200 by default, which is correct on both parts. Declare Variant::Max22200A only when the bill of materials says that part is fitted: a selective clear sent to a MAX22200 clears every flag. Call Declared MAX22200A Declared MAX22200 (the default) ReadFaults() Reads FAULT, clears nothing Reads FAULT; a MAX22200 clears every flag (unavoidable), a MAX22200A none ClearFaults() Reads FAULT, clears every flag The same ClearFaults(which) Clears only the flags in which (Figure 8) Unsupported , nothing sent Both return the flags as they were before the clear. An OCP channel was switched off by the chip; after the flag is cleared it resumes only once it is switched off in ONCH and on again ("Overcurrent Protection (OCP)"). OLF also clears when the channel switches on, HHF when it starts a new cycle. ReadFaultPin() reads the FAULT pin through the optional GpioRead() hook, with no SPI: use it in the deferred part of a FAULT interrupt, then ReadFaults() for the details. GetLastStatusByte() returns STATUS[7:0] as the chip clocked it out during the last command byte, for free. The latch of clear-on-read flags ¶ A STATUS read clears OVT and UVM, and a FAULT read on the MAX22200 clears every flag, whoever makes the read: your ReadStatus() , but also the read-back of SetPairMode() or SetFaultMask() with Verify::ReadBack , a raw ReadRegister() or the start-up's own reads. So that no internal read hides a flag, the driver ORs what each read took from the chip into one latch (handbook KB-CPP-119): Call I/O What it does GetLatchedFaults() none LatchedFaults : OVT and UVM seen by any 32-bit STATUS read, the summary flags of every fault byte, the FAULT flags any FAULT read cleared, and lost when a read that clears flags did not deliver them, since the last clear ClearLatchedFaults() none Empties the latch; the chip is not touched GetStartupFaults() none The FAULT flags the last start-up found and cleared Only ClearLatchedFaults() empties the latch; a restart does not, so the UVM of a DeviceReset survives the EnsureInitialized() that follows. The start-up's STATUS reads feed it too, except for UVM before the wake has completed (Figure 6 reads STATUS to clear the power-on UVM). The chip clears some flags by itself: OLF when the channel switches on (p21), HHF when it starts a new cycle (p23). So that such a flag is not lost before a FAULT read sees it, the summary flags (OVT, UVM, OCP, OLF, HHF, DPM) of every fault byte any access clocks out, the one-transfer switch included, go into the latch as overtemperature , undervoltage , overcurrent , open_load , hit_not_reached and plunger , at no extra I/O; the channel is known only if a FAULT read caught it in faults . A reply that a floating SDO produces (all ones with a 0xFF fault byte) is not data and is never latched as flags; a STATUS read, or a FAULT read that clears, that gets one or fails sets lost : what the chip held is unknown (a genuine FAULT of all ones with a 0xFF fault byte reads the same way, and is treated the same). An 8-bit read (ONCH, HOLD) returns neither OVT nor UVM, and the datasheet does not say it clears them: the driver assumes it does not. On a part declared Variant::Max22200A , ReadFaults() clears nothing and latches nothing; ClearFaults(which) latches the flags in which . Raw register access ¶ ReadRegister(bank) reads one register once: one 32-bit read, 2 transfers, no retry, no decoding and no check (handbook KB-CPP-129), for bring-up and diagnostics. Its side effects are the chip's own: reading STATUS clears OVT and UVM, reading FAULT clears every flag on the MAX22200; both go to the latch. GetLastStatusByte() holds the fault byte of the last access. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( max22200 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case max22200 :: Error :: NoDevice : case max22200 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check SDO pull-up, SDI, CSB, CMD, ENABLE and VM" ; case max22200 :: Error :: Pin : return "the port could not drive CMD or ENABLE" ; case max22200 :: Error :: CommunicationError : return "the chip counted the wrong number of clocks: check SCK and CSB" ; case max22200 :: Error :: ChannelsActive : return "switch the channels off first" ; case max22200 :: Error :: Uncertain : return "a write's reply failed: write the pair mode again or read it back" ; case max22200 :: Error :: Ok : case max22200 :: Error :: NotInitialized : case max22200 :: Error :: InvalidArgument : case max22200 :: Error :: Bus : case max22200 :: Error :: Timeout : case max22200 :: Error :: Crc : case max22200 :: Error :: Busy : case max22200 :: Error :: DeviceFault : case max22200 :: Error :: Unsupported : case max22200 :: Error :: WriteMismatch : case max22200 :: Error :: Undervoltage : case max22200 :: Error :: DeviceReset : default : break ; } return max22200 :: ToString ( e ); } Error Returned by What to do NotInitialized Every I/O call before the start, after Deinitialize() or DeviceReset Call EnsureInitialized() InvalidArgument Any call with an argument out of range; nothing was sent Fix the argument Bus Any I/O call whose transfer failed Retry; the chip may or may not hold the write Pin Any I/O call whose CMD or ENABLE write failed; ReadFaultPin() Check the port's GPIO NoDevice , DeviceIdMismatch EnsureInitialized() Check the wiring ( Troubleshooting ) WriteMismatch EnsureInitialized() ; setters with Verify::ReadBack Retry the write; check the TRIG pins for a mode change CommunicationError EnsureInitialized() ; any call on a running driver that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 Check SCK and CSB; call ApplyConfig() or the setter again: a write may not have landed Undervoltage , Timeout EnsureInitialized() Check VM; retry, raise Config::wake_timeout_us , or cycle VM ChannelsActive ConfigureChannel() , SetPairMode() , ApplyConfig() Switch the channels off first DeviceReset Any I/O call on a running driver Call EnsureInitialized() : the chip lost its configuration Uncertain A switch-on with SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() or SetBridge() in a pair whose mode a failed write left unknown (a switch-off always goes out) Write the pair mode again, or read it back with Verify::ReadBack Unsupported ReadFaultPin() without GpioRead() ; ClearFaults(which) on the MAX22200 Add the hook; clear all What every call checks ¶ Every command byte clocks out the fault byte STATUS[7:0] (Figure 7), and so does an 8-bit write's data byte (Figure 12). On a running driver each one is checked at no extra I/O: A power-on reset. ACTIVE is only ever written 1 while running, so a fault byte with ACTIVE = 0 (other than 0xFF, what a floating SDO reads) means a UVLO reset every register to its default: ACTIVE = 0, every channel off, every CFG_CHn in CDR on the low side ("Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO)", p22; p26, p38-39). The access stops before its data phase, so nothing from the driver's copy goes to the reset chip: no setter re-activates it with the old ONCH over reset channel settings. The driver marks itself uninitialised, every channel off, and returns DeviceReset . A STATUS value with ACTIVE = 0 does the same. An SDO stuck low reads as such a byte: the driver stops, the safe side. A miscounted write. COMER going from 0 to 1 (p34) means a write since the last fault byte with COMER clear was ignored. The call that sees it returns CommunicationError , once (a call that fails for another reason leaves it for the next). The ONCH bits those writes changed count as on for the ChannelsActive check, the channels they configured as of either drive mode, and ApplyConfig() writes their registers again. COMER is read only and may stay set (p36), which would hide every later miscount. So the start-up clears a COMER the wake left by taking ENABLE low for tDIS and high for tEN (the registers survive it, p14; 2 more transfers and the waits, only then), and while COMER is set on a running driver every switch-off is read back: 2 more transfers per switch-off, only in that state. A switch-off is never Ok without proof that it landed. A configuration write (CFG_CHn, HOLD, STATUS, CFG_DPM) whose command byte shows a new COMER stops before its data phase and returns CommunicationError : the channels in doubt may be on, and the chip would ignore a drive-mode change (5c). An ONCH write is never stopped. Doubt a write settles (a switch-off, a STATUS write) stays recorded until a clean fault byte or a read-back proves that write, so a miscount of that very write brings it back. While COMER stays set, ConfigureChannel() reads its write back too (2 more transfers), and the other configuration writes leave what they changed in doubt. IsMiscountDetectionDegraded() (no I/O) says when the driver is in that state. All-ones read data. It carries no fault byte. A reset between a read's command byte and its data leaves the chip without a command and SDO floating, so the driver sends one more command byte (an 8-bit ONCH read, 2 transfers, only after all-ones data): its fault byte tells a reset from a value. Flags the chip clears by itself go to the latch (above). A write whose reply failed ¶ A transfer that fails may still have reached the chip, so after Bus or Pin from a write the chip may hold the old value or the new one. The driver keeps the old value in its copy (it is what the next write is computed from) and treats each cached field so that no decision rests on a guess: Cached field After a failed write Settled by ONCH ( GetChannelsOn() ) The copy keeps the old mask; the bits the write would have changed count as on for ChannelsActive A successful ONCH or STATUS write CMxy (pair modes) A changed pair's mode is unknown: a switch-on in that pair returns Uncertain with no I/O, a switch-off clears both of its bits (only "both off" means the same in every mode, Tables 6 and 7), and a pair-mode change waits for the pair to be off A STATUS write with the pair off, or a STATUS read-back FREQM Unknown: ConfigureChannel() accepts only a channel valid at both master clocks A STATUS write or read-back Fault masks No decision depends on them; STATUS is written again by the next ApplyConfig() A STATUS write CFG_CHn (drive mode, side, HFS, HOLD) The channel may run either mode: any write to it, the copy's own value included, waits for every channel to be off (only then does the chip take the mode bits, step 5c), HOLD is checked against both modes, and ApplyConfig() writes it again A ConfigureChannel() or ApplyConfig() with every channel off CFG_DPM No decision depends on it; written again by the next ApplyConfig() A successful SetDpm() The same handling applies to the writes a new COMER puts in doubt. Crc , Busy and DeviceFault belong to the shared base set and are never returned: the chip sends no CRC, it is never busy to SPI, and its faults are data, never a failed call. Shut down ¶ void PowerDown ( Chip & chip ) { if ( auto r = chip . Deinitialize (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "MAX22200 shutdown failed: %s \n " , max22200 :: ToString ( r . error )); } } Deinitialize() writes STATUS with every channel off and ACTIVE = 0 (outputs Hi-Z), then drives ENABLE low (sleep, under 11 µA). The driver is uninitialised afterwards even if a write failed, and ENABLE goes low whatever happened.

docs.text: One object per chip: max22200::MAX22200<YourPort> chip(port, config); . The constructor stores the configuration and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the only call that starts the chip. Every other call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized until it has succeeded. Every fallible call returns Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion) before reading value ; on failure value is T{} and error says why. A call sends only what the datasheet needs. Calls that can read back take a trailing Verify verify = Verify::None ; Verify::ReadBack reads the register back and compares it, and its cost is stated per call. The driver keeps a copy of every register it wrote. GetConfig() and GetChannelsOn() cost nothing. Call Transfers With Verify::ReadBack SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() , SetBridge() 1 right after an ONCH write with nothing in between, else 2 3 or 4 SetHoldCode() 2 4 ConfigureChannel() , SetPairMode() , SetFaultMask() , SetDpm() 2 4 ReadStatus() , ReadFaults() , ClearFaults() , ReadChannelConfig() , ReadChannelsOn() 2 EnsureInitialized() 42 (+2 per extra wake-up poll) ApplyConfig() 2 per register that changes Deinitialize() 2 A transfer is one CSB-low period: the command byte, or the 1 or 4 data bytes after it.
docs.title: The shape of the API

docs.text: max22200 :: Error BringUp ( Chip & chip ) { // The one entry point: starts the chip on the first call, then returns Ok with no I/O. After a // failure the next call starts again from the beginning. const auto r = chip . EnsureInitialized (); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "MAX22200 init: %s \n " , max22200 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } EnsureInitialized() drives CMD high (its idle level) and ENABLE high, waits tEN (0.5 ms), then runs the programming procedure of Figure 6: it reads STATUS (which clears UVM), then wakes the chip ("wake-up completed?"): a bare ACTIVE = 1 write, tWU (2.5 ms), a STATUS read, repeated every kWakePollUs (10 ms) until ACTIVE reads 1 with UVM clear, for at most Config::wake_timeout_us (100 ms by default). Then it writes STATUS (fault masks, FREQM, pair modes, every channel off, ACTIVE = 1), CFG_CH0 to CFG_CH7 and CFG_DPM. Then it checks what it wrote: STATUS must hold it and every 32-bit write must have echoed its command byte (Figure 10). Next it reads FAULT with every SDI bit high, which clears every flag on both parts: the chip may keep FAULT across an ENABLE cycle (the datasheet does not say ENABLE low clears it), so flags from before the start would hold the FAULT pin and look new. They are reported by GetStartupFaults() . Last, every configuration register read back must equal what was written (CFG_DPM: bits 14:0; bits 31:15 are reserved, some read only with no reset value). COMER is read only and the datasheet does not say what clears it, and a wake write the chip rejected can set it: if it is set when the wake ends, ENABLE goes low for tDIS and high for tEN and STATUS is read again, kStartAttempts times at most (if it stays set, the attempt relies on the read-back and the session reads every switch-off back); a COMER that appears later repeats the procedure, after ENABLE low for tDIS and high again for tEN, up to kStartAttempts times; if every attempt fails, cycle VM. At the wake timeout it returns Undervoltage (UVM still set) or Timeout (UVM clear, ACTIVE still 0), uninitialised, every channel off, ENABLE left high so a retry continues the wake. On any other failure it drives ENABLE low again. It takes 48 transfers when the chip wakes at the first poll, 4 more per extra poll. Error Meaning InvalidArgument The Config fails Validate() ; nothing was sent Bus , Pin The port failed a transfer or a pin write NoDevice SDO read 0xFF throughout: nothing drives it DeviceIdMismatch STATUS read back differs, or a write did not echo its command: SDI, CMD or CSB broken WriteMismatch A configuration register did not take its write Undervoltage UVM still set at Config::wake_timeout_us : VM below UVLO, slow, or UVM stuck (cycle VM) Timeout ACTIVE never read 1 within Config::wake_timeout_us , UVM clear: cycle VM CommunicationError A new COMER in every attempt: the chip miscounts the clocks
docs.title: Start

docs.text: max22200 :: Error ApplyValveMask ( Chip & chip , uint8_t want , bool safety_critical ) { // Every channel at once: one 8-bit write. ReadBack adds one 8-bit read and a compare; use it // where a lost frame matters more than the two transfers. const auto verify = safety_critical ? max22200 :: Verify :: ReadBack : max22200 :: Verify :: None ; return chip . SetChannelsOn ( want , verify ). error ; } max22200 :: Error OpenOne ( Chip & chip , uint8_t channel ) { // From the driver's copy of ONCH: no STATUS read first (it would clear OVT and UVM). return chip . SetChannel ( channel , true ). error ; } SetChannelsOn(mask) writes ONCH, STATUS[31:24], in one 8-bit write (Programming Procedure, step 5a). SetChannel(channel, on) computes the new mask from the driver's copy and sends the same single write: no STATUS read first. GetChannelsOn() returns the copy. A channel with trigger_pin follows its TRIG pin instead. The Command Register stays in force until it is rewritten (p25), so a switch right after a switch sends only its data byte: 1 transfer . The first switch after anything else sends the command again (2 transfers): after any other register access, a failed transfer or pin write, an ENABLE change ( Deinitialize() , a restart), a COMER in a fault byte, or a Verify::ReadBack (its read changes the command). The data byte's SDO carries STATUS[7:0] (Figure 12), kept in GetLastStatusByte() : watching the fault flags costs nothing. If that byte is 0xFF (no answer: a chip that lost the command in a reset clocks nothing out), the write goes out again with its command, so the command byte shows whether the chip was reset. A miscounted write shows as COMER from the next byte on: the call that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 returns CommunicationError (see What every call checks ); only Verify::ReadBack proves that a given switch landed. With Verify::ReadBack the driver reads ONCH back (8 bits) and compares it: WriteMismatch when the chip did not take it (the copy then takes the value read, and the channels that differ are not trusted for the ChannelsActive check), CommunicationError when the read's fault byte shows COMER (the write had the wrong clock count). The copy changes only when the write went out; after Bus the channels the write would have changed count as on for the ChannelsActive check until a write succeeds. ReadChannelsOn() reads ONCH from the chip without changing the copy. A switch-on in a pair whose mode a failed write left unknown returns Uncertain and sends nothing (see A write whose reply failed ). A switch-off is never refused: in such a pair it switches both channels off, the partner too, because ONCHx = ONCHy = 0 is off in every mode (Tables 6 and 7) and one bit alone could turn a full-bridge Brake into Forward or Reverse. SetBridge(pair, BridgeState::HiZ) does the same. A SetChannelsOn() mask that changes such a pair switches it off; if it asked for a switch-on there, the rest of the mask, every switch-off in it, still goes out, then the call returns Uncertain . The pair goes off rather than keep the copy's bits: after a miscount the copy may show a channel on that the chip has off. A channel that may still be on (a failed write may have switched it on, or no clean fault byte has vouched for its switch-off yet) is always switched off when the mask asks it off, even when the copy already says off. In a full-bridge pair SetChannel(ch, false) sets HiZ (both bits 0, Table 7): the partner goes off too. In a parallel pair both ONCH bits move together; in a full-bridge pair use SetBridge(pair, state) (Table 7): BridgeState OUTx OUTy HiZ Hi-Z Hi-Z Forward VM regulated with CFG_CHy Reverse regulated with CFG_CHx VM Brake ground ground
docs.title: Switch channels

docs.text: ConfigureChannel(channel, config) writes the whole CFG_CHn (32 bits). Everything but the drive mode and the side can change while the channel runs (step 5c): the currents, the HIT time, the chopping frequency, SRC, the diagnostics. A change of drive mode or side while any channel is on returns ChannelsActive and sends nothing. max22200 :: Error LowerHold ( Chip & chip , uint8_t channel ) { // On the fly, while the channel holds: one 8-bit write of HFS and HOLD. const auto code = max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 150 , chip . GetConfig (). rref_ohm , chip . GetConfig (). channels [ channel ]. half_scale ); if ( ! code ) { return code . error ; // below the resolution or above 126/128 x IFS } return chip . SetHoldCode ( channel , code . value ). error ; } SetHoldCode(channel, code) writes only CFG_CHn[31:24], HFS and HOLD, in one 8-bit write (step 5b), for a HOLD current controlled on the fly; HFS is kept. The code is checked against the channel's drive mode ( ValidCode() ). SetPairMode() , SetFaultMask() and SetDpm() write STATUS or CFG_DPM; a pair mode changes only with both channels of the pair off. ApplyConfig() writes every register of a new Config that differs from the current one.
docs.title: Change a channel's settings

docs.text: void ServiceFaults ( Chip & chip ) { const auto s = chip . ReadStatus (); // clears OVT and UVM if ( ! s ) { if ( s . error == max22200 :: Error :: DeviceReset ) { ( void ) chip . EnsureInitialized (); // power-on reset: configure the chip again } return ; } if ( ! s . value . overcurrent && ! s . value . open_load && ! s . value . hit_not_reached && ! s . value . plunger ) { return ; } const auto f = chip . ClearFaults (); // returns the flags it cleared if ( f && f . value . overcurrent != 0U ) { // OCP switched those channels off: switch them off, then on again when it is safe. const uint32_t on = chip . GetChannelsOn (); const auto keep = static_cast < uint8_t > ( on & ~ static_cast < uint32_t > ( f . value . overcurrent )); ( void ) chip . SetChannelsOn ( keep ); } } ReadStatus() returns ONCH, the seven flags and ACTIVE. The read clears OVT and UVM on the chip (Register Details: "Read Clears All"); the four channel flags (OCP, OLF, HHF, DPM) say only that some channel has one: the FAULT register says which. If ACTIVE reads 0 on a running driver, a power-on reset cleared every register: the driver marks itself uninitialised and returns DeviceReset ; call EnsureInitialized() to configure the chip again. Every other call does the same from its command byte (see What every call checks ). Config::variant is Variant::Max22200 by default, which is correct on both parts. Declare Variant::Max22200A only when the bill of materials says that part is fitted: a selective clear sent to a MAX22200 clears every flag. Call Declared MAX22200A Declared MAX22200 (the default) ReadFaults() Reads FAULT, clears nothing Reads FAULT; a MAX22200 clears every flag (unavoidable), a MAX22200A none ClearFaults() Reads FAULT, clears every flag The same ClearFaults(which) Clears only the flags in which (Figure 8) Unsupported , nothing sent Both return the flags as they were before the clear. An OCP channel was switched off by the chip; after the flag is cleared it resumes only once it is switched off in ONCH and on again ("Overcurrent Protection (OCP)"). OLF also clears when the channel switches on, HHF when it starts a new cycle. ReadFaultPin() reads the FAULT pin through the optional GpioRead() hook, with no SPI: use it in the deferred part of a FAULT interrupt, then ReadFaults() for the details. GetLastStatusByte() returns STATUS[7:0] as the chip clocked it out during the last command byte, for free.
docs.title: Read and clear faults

docs.text: A STATUS read clears OVT and UVM, and a FAULT read on the MAX22200 clears every flag, whoever makes the read: your ReadStatus() , but also the read-back of SetPairMode() or SetFaultMask() with Verify::ReadBack , a raw ReadRegister() or the start-up's own reads. So that no internal read hides a flag, the driver ORs what each read took from the chip into one latch (handbook KB-CPP-119): Call I/O What it does GetLatchedFaults() none LatchedFaults : OVT and UVM seen by any 32-bit STATUS read, the summary flags of every fault byte, the FAULT flags any FAULT read cleared, and lost when a read that clears flags did not deliver them, since the last clear ClearLatchedFaults() none Empties the latch; the chip is not touched GetStartupFaults() none The FAULT flags the last start-up found and cleared Only ClearLatchedFaults() empties the latch; a restart does not, so the UVM of a DeviceReset survives the EnsureInitialized() that follows. The start-up's STATUS reads feed it too, except for UVM before the wake has completed (Figure 6 reads STATUS to clear the power-on UVM). The chip clears some flags by itself: OLF when the channel switches on (p21), HHF when it starts a new cycle (p23). So that such a flag is not lost before a FAULT read sees it, the summary flags (OVT, UVM, OCP, OLF, HHF, DPM) of every fault byte any access clocks out, the one-transfer switch included, go into the latch as overtemperature , undervoltage , overcurrent , open_load , hit_not_reached and plunger , at no extra I/O; the channel is known only if a FAULT read caught it in faults . A reply that a floating SDO produces (all ones with a 0xFF fault byte) is not data and is never latched as flags; a STATUS read, or a FAULT read that clears, that gets one or fails sets lost : what the chip held is unknown (a genuine FAULT of all ones with a 0xFF fault byte reads the same way, and is treated the same). An 8-bit read (ONCH, HOLD) returns neither OVT nor UVM, and the datasheet does not say it clears them: the driver assumes it does not. On a part declared Variant::Max22200A , ReadFaults() clears nothing and latches nothing; ClearFaults(which) latches the flags in which .
docs.title: The latch of clear-on-read flags

docs.text: ReadRegister(bank) reads one register once: one 32-bit read, 2 transfers, no retry, no decoding and no check (handbook KB-CPP-129), for bring-up and diagnostics. Its side effects are the chip's own: reading STATUS clears OVT and UVM, reading FAULT clears every flag on the MAX22200; both go to the latch. GetLastStatusByte() holds the fault byte of the last access.
docs.title: Raw register access

docs.text: const char * Describe ( max22200 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case max22200 :: Error :: NoDevice : case max22200 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "check SDO pull-up, SDI, CSB, CMD, ENABLE and VM" ; case max22200 :: Error :: Pin : return "the port could not drive CMD or ENABLE" ; case max22200 :: Error :: CommunicationError : return "the chip counted the wrong number of clocks: check SCK and CSB" ; case max22200 :: Error :: ChannelsActive : return "switch the channels off first" ; case max22200 :: Error :: Uncertain : return "a write's reply failed: write the pair mode again or read it back" ; case max22200 :: Error :: Ok : case max22200 :: Error :: NotInitialized : case max22200 :: Error :: InvalidArgument : case max22200 :: Error :: Bus : case max22200 :: Error :: Timeout : case max22200 :: Error :: Crc : case max22200 :: Error :: Busy : case max22200 :: Error :: DeviceFault : case max22200 :: Error :: Unsupported : case max22200 :: Error :: WriteMismatch : case max22200 :: Error :: Undervoltage : case max22200 :: Error :: DeviceReset : default : break ; } return max22200 :: ToString ( e ); } Error Returned by What to do NotInitialized Every I/O call before the start, after Deinitialize() or DeviceReset Call EnsureInitialized() InvalidArgument Any call with an argument out of range; nothing was sent Fix the argument Bus Any I/O call whose transfer failed Retry; the chip may or may not hold the write Pin Any I/O call whose CMD or ENABLE write failed; ReadFaultPin() Check the port's GPIO NoDevice , DeviceIdMismatch EnsureInitialized() Check the wiring ( Troubleshooting ) WriteMismatch EnsureInitialized() ; setters with Verify::ReadBack Retry the write; check the TRIG pins for a mode change CommunicationError EnsureInitialized() ; any call on a running driver that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 Check SCK and CSB; call ApplyConfig() or the setter again: a write may not have landed Undervoltage , Timeout EnsureInitialized() Check VM; retry, raise Config::wake_timeout_us , or cycle VM ChannelsActive ConfigureChannel() , SetPairMode() , ApplyConfig() Switch the channels off first DeviceReset Any I/O call on a running driver Call EnsureInitialized() : the chip lost its configuration Uncertain A switch-on with SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() or SetBridge() in a pair whose mode a failed write left unknown (a switch-off always goes out) Write the pair mode again, or read it back with Verify::ReadBack Unsupported ReadFaultPin() without GpioRead() ; ClearFaults(which) on the MAX22200 Add the hook; clear all
docs.title: Handle errors

docs.text: Every command byte clocks out the fault byte STATUS[7:0] (Figure 7), and so does an 8-bit write's data byte (Figure 12). On a running driver each one is checked at no extra I/O: A power-on reset. ACTIVE is only ever written 1 while running, so a fault byte with ACTIVE = 0 (other than 0xFF, what a floating SDO reads) means a UVLO reset every register to its default: ACTIVE = 0, every channel off, every CFG_CHn in CDR on the low side ("Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO)", p22; p26, p38-39). The access stops before its data phase, so nothing from the driver's copy goes to the reset chip: no setter re-activates it with the old ONCH over reset channel settings. The driver marks itself uninitialised, every channel off, and returns DeviceReset . A STATUS value with ACTIVE = 0 does the same. An SDO stuck low reads as such a byte: the driver stops, the safe side. A miscounted write. COMER going from 0 to 1 (p34) means a write since the last fault byte with COMER clear was ignored. The call that sees it returns CommunicationError , once (a call that fails for another reason leaves it for the next). The ONCH bits those writes changed count as on for the ChannelsActive check, the channels they configured as of either drive mode, and ApplyConfig() writes their registers again. COMER is read only and may stay set (p36), which would hide every later miscount. So the start-up clears a COMER the wake left by taking ENABLE low for tDIS and high for tEN (the registers survive it, p14; 2 more transfers and the waits, only then), and while COMER is set on a running driver every switch-off is read back: 2 more transfers per switch-off, only in that state. A switch-off is never Ok without proof that it landed. A configuration write (CFG_CHn, HOLD, STATUS, CFG_DPM) whose command byte shows a new COMER stops before its data phase and returns CommunicationError : the channels in doubt may be on, and the chip would ignore a drive-mode change (5c). An ONCH write is never stopped. Doubt a write settles (a switch-off, a STATUS write) stays recorded until a clean fault byte or a read-back proves that write, so a miscount of that very write brings it back. While COMER stays set, ConfigureChannel() reads its write back too (2 more transfers), and the other configuration writes leave what they changed in doubt. IsMiscountDetectionDegraded() (no I/O) says when the driver is in that state. All-ones read data. It carries no fault byte. A reset between a read's command byte and its data leaves the chip without a command and SDO floating, so the driver sends one more command byte (an 8-bit ONCH read, 2 transfers, only after all-ones data): its fault byte tells a reset from a value. Flags the chip clears by itself go to the latch (above).
docs.title: What every call checks

docs.text: A transfer that fails may still have reached the chip, so after Bus or Pin from a write the chip may hold the old value or the new one. The driver keeps the old value in its copy (it is what the next write is computed from) and treats each cached field so that no decision rests on a guess: Cached field After a failed write Settled by ONCH ( GetChannelsOn() ) The copy keeps the old mask; the bits the write would have changed count as on for ChannelsActive A successful ONCH or STATUS write CMxy (pair modes) A changed pair's mode is unknown: a switch-on in that pair returns Uncertain with no I/O, a switch-off clears both of its bits (only "both off" means the same in every mode, Tables 6 and 7), and a pair-mode change waits for the pair to be off A STATUS write with the pair off, or a STATUS read-back FREQM Unknown: ConfigureChannel() accepts only a channel valid at both master clocks A STATUS write or read-back Fault masks No decision depends on them; STATUS is written again by the next ApplyConfig() A STATUS write CFG_CHn (drive mode, side, HFS, HOLD) The channel may run either mode: any write to it, the copy's own value included, waits for every channel to be off (only then does the chip take the mode bits, step 5c), HOLD is checked against both modes, and ApplyConfig() writes it again A ConfigureChannel() or ApplyConfig() with every channel off CFG_DPM No decision depends on it; written again by the next ApplyConfig() A successful SetDpm() The same handling applies to the writes a new COMER puts in doubt. Crc , Busy and DeviceFault belong to the shared base set and are never returned: the chip sends no CRC, it is never busy to SPI, and its faults are data, never a failed call.
docs.title: A write whose reply failed

docs.text: void PowerDown ( Chip & chip ) { if ( auto r = chip . Deinitialize (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "MAX22200 shutdown failed: %s \n " , max22200 :: ToString ( r . error )); } } Deinitialize() writes STATUS with every channel off and ACTIVE = 0 (outputs Hi-Z), then drives ENABLE low (sleep, under 11 µA). The driver is uninitialised afterwards even if a write failed, and ENABLE goes low whatever happened.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, the two-phase access every call is made of, and the copy of the chip's registers the driver keeps. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: The SPI, the 8-bit accesses and the daisy chain: SPI Detailed Description; Figure 5, p. 23 The programming procedure: Programming Procedure; Figure 6, p. 23 The Command Register and the fault byte: Command Register Description (COMMAND); Table 9; Figure 7, p. 25 32-bit and 8-bit transfers and the command echo: Reading and Writing Operations of Registers; Figures 10 to 13, p. 30 Register map and reset values: Register Map; Register Details, p. 35 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/max22200.hpp public calls ; inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Core inc/max22200.hpp , src/max22200.ipp Lifecycle, the programming procedure, the register copy, the checks, errors Types and registers inc/max22200_types.hpp , inc/max22200_registers.hpp Error , Result<T> , Config , the encodings, the unit conversions, Validate() ; the register map Port contract inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp The CRTP base, CtrlPin and GpioSignal , the SpiPort concept, the two-phase access Platform port Your class Bus bring-up, byte transfers, CMD and ENABLE, the delay; optionally the FAULT pin and logging Kconfig layer inc/max22200_kconfig.hpp Optional: a Config from ESP-IDF menuconfig One access, two transfers ¶ The chip has one 8-bit Command Register and four kinds of 32-bit register: STATUS, CFG_CH0 to CFG_CH7, FAULT and CFG_DPM. Every access is two SPI transfers ("Command Register Description", Figures 7 and 10 to 13): Transfer CMD SDI SDO 1. Command high, also at the CSB rising edge RB/W, A_BNK (bank), 8bit/n32bits STATUS[7:0], the fault byte 2a. Write 32 bits low DATAIN[7:0], [15:8], [23:16], [31:24]: LSB byte first STATUS[7:0], the command, 0, 0 2b. Read 32 bits low 0 (FAULT: the flags to clear, LSB byte first) DATA[31:24], [23:16], [15:8], [7:0]: MSB byte first 2c. Write 8 bits low DATAIN[31:24] STATUS[7:0] 2d. Read 8 bits low DATA[31:24] detail::RegisterBus does this and nothing else. It drives CMD high only if the port can (a command sent with CMD low would be taken as data), and drives it low again after every command byte. The fault byte of every command is kept ( GetLastStatusByte() ); the command echo of a 32-bit write is checked at start-up and with Verify::ReadBack . The 8-bit accesses are the fast paths the datasheet names: ONCH (switching, SetChannelsOn() ) and HFS/HOLD ( SetHoldCode() ), one byte each. One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as MAX22200<Port> participant Port as Your port App->>Core: SetChannel(2, true) Note over Core: next = copy of ONCH | 0x04 Core->>Port: GpioSet(Cmd, ACTIVE) Core->>Port: Transfer(0x81): write STATUS, 8 bit Port-->>Core: true, fault byte Core->>Port: GpioSet(Cmd, INACTIVE) Core->>Port: Transfer(next) Port-->>Core: true Note over Core: copy of ONCH = next Core-->>App: Result<void>{Ok} The register copy ¶ The driver keeps what it wrote: the Config (STATUS fields, every CFG_CHn, CFG_DPM) and ONCH. It needs the copy because: STATUS holds ONCH and the configuration together, so a 32-bit STATUS write (a pair mode, the masks) must carry the current ONCH, and a single-channel switch must know the other seven without reading STATUS. A read would cost two transfers and clear OVT and UVM as a side effect (every STATUS read the driver does make keeps them in the latch of GetLatchedFaults() ). The chip ignores a drive-mode or side change while a channel is on, and a pair-mode change while one of the pair is on; the driver refuses them up front ( ChannelsActive ) from the copy. After a failed ONCH write the channels it would have changed count as on for this check, because the chip may have taken the write. The 8-bit HOLD write must carry the channel's HFS bit. The copy is what the driver wrote, not what the chip holds: ReadStatus() , ReadChannelsOn() , ReadChannelConfig() and Verify::ReadBack read the chip. Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the SpiPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Required pins in the port. CMD is part of the protocol, so GpioSet() is required and must return bool ; a failed pin write is reported as Pin , never ignored. Optional hooks by requires . GpioRead (the FAULT pin) and Log are detected with C++20 requires in one place; without them ReadFaultPin() returns Unsupported and nothing is logged. Codes, not floats, in the configuration. ChannelConfig holds the register's codes; the conversions from milliamps and microseconds are exact integer functions that refuse a value the chip cannot do safely. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state. docs.title: Layers

docs.text: The chip has one 8-bit Command Register and four kinds of 32-bit register: STATUS, CFG_CH0 to CFG_CH7, FAULT and CFG_DPM. Every access is two SPI transfers ("Command Register Description", Figures 7 and 10 to 13): Transfer CMD SDI SDO 1. Command high, also at the CSB rising edge RB/W, A_BNK (bank), 8bit/n32bits STATUS[7:0], the fault byte 2a. Write 32 bits low DATAIN[7:0], [15:8], [23:16], [31:24]: LSB byte first STATUS[7:0], the command, 0, 0 2b. Read 32 bits low 0 (FAULT: the flags to clear, LSB byte first) DATA[31:24], [23:16], [15:8], [7:0]: MSB byte first 2c. Write 8 bits low DATAIN[31:24] STATUS[7:0] 2d. Read 8 bits low DATA[31:24] detail::RegisterBus does this and nothing else. It drives CMD high only if the port can (a command sent with CMD low would be taken as data), and drives it low again after every command byte. The fault byte of every command is kept ( GetLastStatusByte() ); the command echo of a 32-bit write is checked at start-up and with Verify::ReadBack . The 8-bit accesses are the fast paths the datasheet names: ONCH (switching, SetChannelsOn() ) and HFS/HOLD ( SetHoldCode() ), one byte each.

docs.text: The driver keeps what it wrote: the Config (STATUS fields, every CFG_CHn, CFG_DPM) and ONCH. It needs the copy because: STATUS holds ONCH and the configuration together, so a 32-bit STATUS write (a pair mode, the masks) must carry the current ONCH, and a single-channel switch must know the other seven without reading STATUS. A read would cost two transfers and clear OVT and UVM as a side effect (every STATUS read the driver does make keeps them in the latch of GetLatchedFaults() ). The chip ignores a drive-mode or side change while a channel is on, and a pair-mode change while one of the pair is on; the driver refuses them up front ( ChannelsActive ) from the copy. After a failed ONCH write the channels it would have changed count as on for this check, because the chip may have taken the write. The 8-bit HOLD write must carry the channel's HFS bit. The copy is what the driver wrote, not what the chip holds: ReadStatus() , ReadChannelsOn() , ReadChannelConfig() and Verify::ReadBack read the chip.
docs.title: The register copy

docs.text: CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the SpiPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. Required pins in the port. CMD is part of the protocol, so GpioSet() is required and must return bool ; a failed pin write is reported as Pin , never ignored. Optional hooks by requires . GpioRead (the FAULT pin) and Log are detected with C++20 requires in one place; without them ReadFaultPin() returns Unsupported and nothing is logged. Codes, not floats, in the configuration. ChannelConfig holds the register's codes; the conversions from milliamps and microseconds are exact integer functions that refuse a value the chip cannot do safely. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state.

docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ The repository moved to kokeb-labs-drivers; URLs follow. [0.1.0] - 2026-11-10 ¶ Breaking ¶ Every I/O call of a running driver can return Error::DeviceReset (was ReadStatus() only): a fault byte or a STATUS value with ACTIVE = 0 means a power-on reset. ReadRegister(reg::kStatus) no longer returns such a STATUS as read. Every I/O call of a running driver can return Error::CommunicationError when it sees COMER go from 0 to 1 (was only with Verify::ReadBack ): an earlier write was miscounted. New Error::Uncertain (23): SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() and SetBridge() refuse a switch-on in a pair whose mode a write with a failed reply left unknown; that pair is switched off instead (the rest of a SetChannelsOn() mask still goes out, and a channel a failed write may have switched on is switched off when asked, even if the copy already says off). A switch-off there is never refused: it switches both channels of the pair off, the partner too. SetChannel(ch, false) in a full-bridge pair sets HiZ (both channels off) instead of returning InvalidArgument . LatchedFaults has new fields ( overcurrent , open_load , hit_not_reached , plunger , lost ), and Any() counts them. FullScaleUa() returns Result<uint32_t> ( InvalidArgument for an RREF out of range, kNoRref included) instead of 0, and HitTimeUs() returns Result<uint32_t> ( InvalidArgument for kHitTimeContinuous ) instead of kForever , which is removed: no public helper returns a sentinel (handbook KB-CPP-126, KB-CPP-127). A load-dependent diagnostic ( open_load_detect , plunger_detect , hit_current_check ) needs its channel in the new Config::loaded_channels ; Validate() , ApplyConfig() , EnsureInitialized() and ConfigureChannel() refuse it otherwise with InvalidArgument (KB-CPP-131). The port concept checks the required hooks exactly: each parameter of EnsureInitialized() , Transfer() and GpioSet() must have exactly the documented type, and each hook must be noexcept and return bool (KB-CPP20-006). GpioSet() is part of SpiPort . A DelayUs() , GpioRead() or Log() declared with another signature is a compile error (KB-CPP20-007). reg::kMaxSpiHz is replaced by kMaxClockHz with the other bus requirements in max22200_spi_interface.hpp . Error is [[nodiscard]] ; GetConfig() is const& -qualified and deleted on a temporary driver. EnsureInitialized() takes 48 transfers (was 46): it reads and clears FAULT. Added ¶ Bus requirements as constexpr (KB-CPP-123): kSpiMode , kMsbFirst , kMaxClockHz , kMinCsHighNs , kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs , kContinuousWord , kCmdSetupNs , kTransferBytes , kSdoOpenDrain , with datasheet references; the host and ESP32 ports and the documented port check their settings with static_assert . A driver-owned latch of clear-on-read flags (KB-CPP-119): every 32-bit STATUS read ORs OVT and UVM into it, every FAULT read the flags it clears; GetLatchedFaults() and ClearLatchedFaults() , no I/O. Only the clear empties it (a restart does not), and a reply a floating SDO produces is never latched (KB-CPP-116). The start-up reads and clears FAULT and reports what was latched before it in GetStartupFaults() (KB-CPP-058). ReadRegister() , a single-shot raw 32-bit read with no retry (KB-CPP-129). DecodePairMode() , ValidLoadDiagnostics() , Faults::Or() and Faults::And() , LatchedFaults . Strict ISO C++20 everywhere (KB-CPP20-001): CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF , -pedantic-errors and the C++20 deprecations as errors; a header self-check per public header on GCC, Clang, the Cortex-M build and inside the ESP-IDF build ( max22200_cxx20_check.cpp ). Compile-fail tests for a narrowed Transfer() length, a Transfer() without noexcept , a DelayUs(uint16_t) , a void GpioRead() , a GpioRead() taking the signal by value and a misdeclared Log() ; tests/test_latch.cpp ; compile-time round trips of the register encoders. The review skills cpp20-profile , misra-review and hardware-lessons-review and the safety-reviewer agent, from the template. First version of the driver for the Analog Devices MAX22200 and MAX22200A octal solenoid and motor drivers, written on the Kokeb Labs driver template from datasheet 19-100531 Rev 1, every rule checked against the datasheet. max22200::MAX22200<Port> with the configuration in the constructor and one start-up call, EnsureInitialized() : CMD high, ENABLE and tEN, the programming procedure of Figure 6 (STATUS read; a wake loop of bare ACTIVE = 1 writes, tWU and STATUS reads until ACTIVE reads 1 with UVM clear, bounded by Config::wake_timeout_us , 100 ms by default; STATUS write, every CFG_CHn and CFG_DPM), and a read-back of every register and of each write's command echo. A wake that runs out returns Undervoltage (UVM set) or Timeout , uninitialised with every channel off. COMER repeats the procedure ( kStartAttempts ). ApplyConfig() writes only what changed; Deinitialize() switches every channel off, clears ACTIVE and drives ENABLE low. Switching from the driver's copy of ONCH, one 8-bit write each: SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() (parallel pairs switch as one), SetBridge() (Table 7); ReadChannelsOn() . The Command Register stays in force until rewritten (p25), so an ONCH write right after another is one transfer (the data byte); any other access, a failure, an ENABLE change, COMER or a read-back sends the command again. The data byte's STATUS[7:0] updates GetLastStatusByte() . Settings: ConfigureChannel() , SetHoldCode() (8-bit HOLD update on the fly), SetPairMode() , SetFaultMask() , SetDpm() ; Verify::ReadBack per call reads the register back and checks COMER. A drive-mode, side or pair-mode change while a channel concerned is on is refused ( Error::ChannelsActive ). Diagnostics: ReadStatus() (power-on reset reported as Error::DeviceReset ), ReadFaults() and ClearFaults() for both parts ( Config::variant , Variant::Max22200 by default: correct on both parts, a selective clear needs Max22200A declared per the BOM and a bench check), ReadFaultPin() through an optional GpioRead() hook, GetLastStatusByte() . After a read-back that differs the driver's copy takes the value read (ONCH, CFG_CH, HOLD, STATUS, CFG_DPM); the ONCH bits that differ stay untrusted, and a channel whose CFG_CH write failed or read back different accepts no write while a channel is on. ChannelConfig and Config as the registers' codes, Config{} equal to the reset state, Validate() and ValidateChannel() with every datasheet rule; exact conversions CurrentCode() , CurrentUa() (IFS / 128), HitTimeCode() , HitTimeUs() , DpmCurrentCode() (IFS / 127), DebounceUs() , ChopPeriodNs() , DutyLimitsOf() ; Kconfig options for the part, the oscillator and RREF. Errors NoDevice , Pin , CommunicationError , WriteMismatch , Undervoltage , ChannelsActive , DeviceReset . Host tests over a protocol model of both parts, written from the datasheet independently of the driver's register header and cross-checked against it, with the bus and board faults the port contract allows, every transfer and pin write of every operation failed in turn; a libFuzzer target with its corpus replayed as a CTest; the host and ESP32 examples; the Drive modes and Status and limitations pages. Not verified on hardware. Datasheet rules the first version applies. Details on the Status and limitations page: CDR currents use IFS / 128 (Table 4); no current becomes code 127, the unregulated full-on state. HIT times use the exact chopping frequency (33.3 kHz, 26.7 kHz, Tables 1 and 5); a HIT time beyond 254 steps is refused instead of becoming "continuous IHIT". COMER is tested as a bit of the fault byte (Figure 6), never by comparing the whole byte. The selective FAULT clear sends its mask LSB byte first, where Figure 8 draws it; not verified on hardware: it is one constant, reg::kFaultClearLsbByteFirst , and a bench step decides. A FAULT read on the MAX22200A clears only what SDI selects. VDR duty codes are sent as asked, so 0 % and 100 % are reachable (Table 3); the chip applies δMIN and δMAX itself. SRC at 50 kHz, CDR, SRC, HFS or DPM on the high side, and HHF in VDR are refused. The start-up wakes the chip with bare ACTIVE writes until ACTIVE reads 1 with UVM clear (Figure 6), bounded by Config::wake_timeout_us . COMER is not assumed to clear on a STATUS read (p36: "Read Only"): it is armed once the wake is done, only a 0 to 1 transition repeats the procedure, and ENABLE goes low for tDIS and high for tEN between attempts. CMD idles high: it is driven high again after every data phase, the one-transfer ONCH write included (p25-26). Config::rref_ohm is not given by default ( kNoRref ): the code-level API works without it, and CurrentCode() , CurrentUa() and DpmCurrentCode() return InvalidArgument until it is set. CFG_DPM is compared on bits 14:0 only: bits 31:15 are reserved, three of them read only with no reset value (p40-41). Mode and pair-mode changes are refused while the channels concerned run (step 5c, Register Details); parallel pairs switch both ONCH bits (Table 6); out-of-range DPM settings are refused instead of clamped; shutdown reports its writes. Changed ¶ Hardware page: the pinout, the block diagram and the application circuit are now figures drawn from docs/hardware.yml , which also generates the pin table (replacing the hand-written one) and the parts table. Every pin, block and part cites the datasheet section and page; values the datasheet does not give are marked as not confirmed. kokeb-docs hardware --kicad-netlist exports the circuit. Synced with the driver template: tools/preflight.sh runs clang-tidy over every file CI lints, as CI does, and the hardware-lessons review adds the switch-off lessons. The fault-handling example in the API guide clears the overcurrent channels with unsigned bit operations, which that clang-tidy run requires. The misra-review , cpp20-profile and new-driver-from-template skills and docs/repo-setup.md follow the template: reading the MISRA report, the known tool misfires, enumeration ranges without a sentinel, and the settings tool. tools/preflight.sh and the verify and hardware-lessons-review skills follow the template: every check CI runs that a workstation can run, in one command, and the rules for device resets, faults the chip clears itself, dropped writes, switch-offs that no uncertainty refuses, channels in doubt and a model that changes state on its own. Follows the driver template's portable ownership: copyright belongs to The driver-max22200 authors ( LICENSE , every source header, driver.yml authors , the docs footer). tools/check_standalone.py runs in the Handbook source checks job and keeps the code and docs about this chip only. AGENTS.md follows the template's structure; the issue and PR templates ask for the board, MCU and port in one field. The port concepts match each hook's address against exactly one noexcept signature with detail::ExactHook<Port, Sig>::Take(&Port::Hook) instead of probing it with a converting detail::Exactly<T> : no conversion operator is left. A misdeclared hook is still a compile error. kAlwaysFalse takes a class and the enumeration helpers an enumeration ( ClassType , Enumeration ), each with a compile-fail test. HasGpioRead matches bool GpioRead(CtrlPin, GpioSignal&) noexcept the same way, so a hook that takes the signal by value or as const& still does not match. Include guards instead of #pragma once in every header (KB-CPP-019). Every narrow operand of a shift or bitwise operator is widened to uint32_t first, and UL literals and unsigned casts are fixed-width (KB-CPP20-020, -021); enumerations are range-checked with detail::IsEnumerator() (KB-CPP20-025); ToString() is a switch over every enumerator. The ESP32 port sets CMD high and ENABLE low before it enables their outputs (KB-HW-018); the Porting page lists each control pin's idle level and polarity. The data phases go through fixed-extent std::span s (KB-CPP20-042). MISRA C++:2023 conformance: integer constant arguments have exactly the parameter's type through the consteval literals detail::operator""_u8 and operator""_u32 ( EncodeStatus(config_, 0_u8, true) , FaultClearSdi(0xFFFF'FFFF_u32) ; an out-of-range literal does not compile), and a narrow ONCH bit is widened explicitly (Rule 7.0.6); the layout checks compare against U literals (Rule 7.0.5); operands of && , || , ?: and comparisons are parenthesised (Rule 8.0.1); every switch over an enumeration ends with default: break; , and the host tests build with -Wswitch-enum so a new enumerator still warns (Rule 9.4.2); the five defaulted operator== are hidden friends (Rule 16.6.1); the .ipp include at the end of max22200.hpp carries the deviation marker of MD-CPP-009 (Rule 19.0.3). Behaviour is unchanged. Synced with driver-template: _config/.clang-tidy (the handbook's high-level profile), the repository checks with the handbook's source checks, the verify , add-driver-feature and new-driver-from-template skills. Fixed ¶ A SetChannelsOn() that returns Uncertain no longer skips its write while a switch-off is unverified: a switch-off that no fault byte with COMER clear has vouched for yet (the chip may have miscounted it, and the next fault byte may have been lost on the bus) counts as possibly on, so a mask that asks that channel off goes out again. Doubt that a write settles is no longer lost when the chip miscounts that very write (p34, p36): a switch-off, a STATUS write that carries ONCH, CMxy or FREQM moves the doubt it clears into the unverified sets, so the COMER that follows restores it; with COMER already set a STATUS write keeps the doubt until a read-back, and a read-back that matches proves every switch. A configuration write (CFG_CHn, HOLD, STATUS, CFG_DPM) whose command byte shows a new COMER stops before its data phase and returns CommunicationError : the channels the miscount left in doubt may be on, so a drive-mode change would be ignored by the chip (Programming Procedure 5c). ONCH writes are never stopped, so a switch-off always goes out. While COMER stays set (detection degraded), ConfigureChannel() reads its write back (2 more transfers), and a CFG_CH or STATUS write without a read-back leaves the channel's mode, or the pair modes and FREQM it changes, in doubt: a miscounted configuration write cannot show then, so it is never trusted. tools/preflight.sh follows the template: clang-tidy runs as CI runs it. A signed-bitwise finding it then reported in the fault-handling example of the API guide is fixed. A power-on reset (UVLO, p22) is detected by every call from the fault byte of its command, before the data phase: no write reaches the reset chip, so no setter re-activates it with the cached ONCH over reset CFG_CHn values. The driver marks itself uninitialised with every channel off and returns DeviceReset . A STATUS value with ACTIVE = 0 does the same. A one-transfer ONCH write that gets no fault byte back (0xFF) sends its command again so the reset shows. Flags the chip clears by itself (OLF on a switch-on, p21; HHF on a new cycle, p23) are no longer lost: the summary flags of every fault byte (OVT, UVM, OCP, OLF, HHF, DPM) go into GetLatchedFaults() at no extra I/O. A miscounted write (COMER, p34) is no longer reported as Ok for ever: the first call that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 returns CommunicationError ; the ONCH bits the writes since the last clean fault byte changed count as on for ChannelsActive , their channels as of either drive mode, and ApplyConfig() writes their registers again. A write whose reply failed may have taken effect: a pair mode or FREQM it changed is unknown until a STATUS write (pair off) or read-back settles it, a switch in that pair returns Uncertain , ConfigureChannel() accepts only a channel valid at both clocks, and ApplyConfig() writes the register again even when the copy matches. A channel that may run either drive mode is written, its own cached value included, only with every channel off, so the write settles the mode. A COMER the wake leaves is cleared at start-up with ENABLE low, and while COMER stays set on a running driver every switch-off is read back (2 more transfers each), so miscount detection never stays off silently; IsMiscountDetectionDegraded() reports that state. A switch-off miscounted in the very call that first shows the COMER keeps its channels in doubt (they count as on and are switched off again when asked), and so does a switch-off whose forced read-back fails. Read data of all ones is followed by one more command byte, so a reset between a read's command byte and its data returns DeviceReset instead of the floating value. A STATUS read, or a FAULT read that clears, that fails or gets a floating reply sets LatchedFaults::lost : the flags it cleared are unknown. A genuine FAULT of 0xFFFFFFFF with a 0xFF fault byte is treated the same, never used as data. A STATUS read-back ( SetPairMode() , SetFaultMask() with Verify::ReadBack ) cleared OVT and UVM on the chip and dropped them; they are kept in the latch. Faults latched before the start held the FAULT pin after a clean start; the start-up now clears them. A STATUS read-back with the reserved CMxy value 3 stored it as a PairMode ; it is refused and the copy keeps its mode. ApplyConfig() on a running driver dropped a new wake_timeout_us ; it is kept, as is the new loaded_channels .

Host tests over a protocol model of both parts, written from the datasheet independently of the driver's register header and cross-checked against it, with the bus and board faults the port contract allows, every transfer and pin write of every operation failed in turn; a libFuzzer target with its corpus replayed as a CTest; the host and ESP32 examples; the Drive modes and Status and limitations pages. Not verified on hardware. Datasheet rules the first version applies. Details on the Status and limitations page: CDR currents use IFS / 128 (Table 4); no current becomes code 127, the unregulated full-on state. HIT times use the exact chopping frequency (33.3 kHz, 26.7 kHz, Tables 1 and 5); a HIT time beyond 254 steps is refused instead of becoming "continuous IHIT". COMER is tested as a bit of the fault byte (Figure 6), never by comparing the whole byte. The selective FAULT clear sends its mask LSB byte first, where Figure 8 draws it; not verified on hardware: it is one constant, reg::kFaultClearLsbByteFirst , and a bench step decides. A FAULT read on the MAX22200A clears only what SDI selects. VDR duty codes are sent as asked, so 0 % and 100 % are reachable (Table 3); the chip applies δMIN and δMAX itself. SRC at 50 kHz, CDR, SRC, HFS or DPM on the high side, and HHF in VDR are refused. The start-up wakes the chip with bare ACTIVE writes until ACTIVE reads 1 with UVM clear (Figure 6), bounded by Config::wake_timeout_us . COMER is not assumed to clear on a STATUS read (p36: "Read Only"): it is armed once the wake is done, only a 0 to 1 transition repeats the procedure, and ENABLE goes low for tDIS and high for tEN between attempts. CMD idles high: it is driven high again after every data phase, the one-transfer ONCH write included (p25-26). Config::rref_ohm is not given by default ( kNoRref ): the code-level API works without it, and CurrentCode() , CurrentUa() and DpmCurrentCode() return InvalidArgument until it is set. CFG_DPM is compared on bits 14:0 only: bits 31:15 are reserved, three of them read only with no reset value (p40-41). Mode and pair-mode changes are refused while the channels concerned run (step 5c, Register Details); parallel pairs switch both ONCH bits (Table 6); out-of-range DPM settings are refused instead of clamped; shutdown reports its writes.
