docs.text: Hardware page: the pinout, the block diagram and the application circuit are now figures drawn from docs/hardware.yml , which also generates the pin table (replacing the hand-written one) and the parts table. Every pin, block and part cites the datasheet section and page; values the datasheet does not give are marked as not confirmed. kokeb-docs hardware --kicad-netlist exports the circuit. Synced with the driver template: tools/preflight.sh runs clang-tidy over every file CI lints, as CI does, and the hardware-lessons review adds the switch-off lessons. The fault-handling example in the API guide clears the overcurrent channels with unsigned bit operations, which that clang-tidy run requires. The misra-review , cpp20-profile and new-driver-from-template skills and docs/repo-setup.md follow the template: reading the MISRA report, the known tool misfires, enumeration ranges without a sentinel, and the settings tool. tools/preflight.sh and the verify and hardware-lessons-review skills follow the template: every check CI runs that a workstation can run, in one command, and the rules for device resets, faults the chip clears itself, dropped writes, switch-offs that no uncertainty refuses, channels in doubt and a model that changes state on its own. Follows the driver template's portable ownership: copyright belongs to The driver-max22200 authors ( LICENSE , every source header, driver.yml authors , the docs footer). tools/check_standalone.py runs in the Handbook source checks job and keeps the code and docs about this chip only. AGENTS.md follows the template's structure; the issue and PR templates ask for the board, MCU and port in one field. The port concepts match each hook's address against exactly one noexcept signature with detail::ExactHook<Port, Sig>::Take(&Port::Hook) instead of probing it with a converting detail::Exactly<T> : no conversion operator is left. A misdeclared hook is still a compile error. kAlwaysFalse takes a class and the enumeration helpers an enumeration ( ClassType , Enumeration ), each with a compile-fail test. HasGpioRead matches bool GpioRead(CtrlPin, GpioSignal&) noexcept the same way, so a hook that takes the signal by value or as const& still does not match. Include guards instead of #pragma once in every header (KB-CPP-019). Every narrow operand of a shift or bitwise operator is widened to uint32_t first, and UL literals and unsigned casts are fixed-width (KB-CPP20-020, -021); enumerations are range-checked with detail::IsEnumerator() (KB-CPP20-025); ToString() is a switch over every enumerator. The ESP32 port sets CMD high and ENABLE low before it enables their outputs (KB-HW-018); the Porting page lists each control pin's idle level and polarity. The data phases go through fixed-extent std::span s (KB-CPP20-042). MISRA C++:2023 conformance: integer constant arguments have exactly the parameter's type through the consteval literals detail::operator""_u8 and operator""_u32 ( EncodeStatus(config_, 0_u8, true) , FaultClearSdi(0xFFFF'FFFF_u32) ; an out-of-range literal does not compile), and a narrow ONCH bit is widened explicitly (Rule 7.0.6); the layout checks compare against U literals (Rule 7.0.5); operands of && , || , ?: and comparisons are parenthesised (Rule 8.0.1); every switch over an enumeration ends with default: break; , and the host tests build with -Wswitch-enum so a new enumerator still warns (Rule 9.4.2); the five defaulted operator== are hidden friends (Rule 16.6.1); the .ipp include at the end of max22200.hpp carries the deviation marker of MD-CPP-009 (Rule 19.0.3). Behaviour is unchanged. Synced with driver-template: _config/.clang-tidy (the handbook's high-level profile), the repository checks with the handbook's source checks, the verify , add-driver-feature and new-driver-from-template skills.

docs.text: A SetChannelsOn() that returns Uncertain no longer skips its write while a switch-off is unverified: a switch-off that no fault byte with COMER clear has vouched for yet (the chip may have miscounted it, and the next fault byte may have been lost on the bus) counts as possibly on, so a mask that asks that channel off goes out again. Doubt that a write settles is no longer lost when the chip miscounts that very write (p34, p36): a switch-off, a STATUS write that carries ONCH, CMxy or FREQM moves the doubt it clears into the unverified sets, so the COMER that follows restores it; with COMER already set a STATUS write keeps the doubt until a read-back, and a read-back that matches proves every switch. A configuration write (CFG_CHn, HOLD, STATUS, CFG_DPM) whose command byte shows a new COMER stops before its data phase and returns CommunicationError : the channels the miscount left in doubt may be on, so a drive-mode change would be ignored by the chip (Programming Procedure 5c). ONCH writes are never stopped, so a switch-off always goes out. While COMER stays set (detection degraded), ConfigureChannel() reads its write back (2 more transfers), and a CFG_CH or STATUS write without a read-back leaves the channel's mode, or the pair modes and FREQM it changes, in doubt: a miscounted configuration write cannot show then, so it is never trusted. tools/preflight.sh follows the template: clang-tidy runs as CI runs it. A signed-bitwise finding it then reported in the fault-handling example of the API guide is fixed. A power-on reset (UVLO, p22) is detected by every call from the fault byte of its command, before the data phase: no write reaches the reset chip, so no setter re-activates it with the cached ONCH over reset CFG_CHn values. The driver marks itself uninitialised with every channel off and returns DeviceReset . A STATUS value with ACTIVE = 0 does the same. A one-transfer ONCH write that gets no fault byte back (0xFF) sends its command again so the reset shows. Flags the chip clears by itself (OLF on a switch-on, p21; HHF on a new cycle, p23) are no longer lost: the summary flags of every fault byte (OVT, UVM, OCP, OLF, HHF, DPM) go into GetLatchedFaults() at no extra I/O. A miscounted write (COMER, p34) is no longer reported as Ok for ever: the first call that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 returns CommunicationError ; the ONCH bits the writes since the last clean fault byte changed count as on for ChannelsActive , their channels as of either drive mode, and ApplyConfig() writes their registers again. A write whose reply failed may have taken effect: a pair mode or FREQM it changed is unknown until a STATUS write (pair off) or read-back settles it, a switch in that pair returns Uncertain , ConfigureChannel() accepts only a channel valid at both clocks, and ApplyConfig() writes the register again even when the copy matches. A channel that may run either drive mode is written, its own cached value included, only with every channel off, so the write settles the mode. A COMER the wake leaves is cleared at start-up with ENABLE low, and while COMER stays set on a running driver every switch-off is read back (2 more transfers each), so miscount detection never stays off silently; IsMiscountDetectionDegraded() reports that state. A switch-off miscounted in the very call that first shows the COMER keeps its channels in doubt (they count as on and are switched off again when asked), and so does a switch-off whose forced read-back fails. Read data of all ones is followed by one more command byte, so a reset between a read's command byte and its data returns DeviceReset instead of the floating value. A STATUS read, or a FAULT read that clears, that fails or gets a floating reply sets LatchedFaults::lost : the flags it cleared are unknown. A genuine FAULT of 0xFFFFFFFF with a 0xFF fault byte is treated the same, never used as data. A STATUS read-back ( SetPairMode() , SetFaultMask() with Verify::ReadBack ) cleared OVT and UVM on the chip and dropped them; they are kept in the latch. Faults latched before the start held the FAULT pin after a clean start; the start-up now clears them. A STATUS read-back with the reserved CMxy value 3 stored it as a PairMode ; it is refused and the copy keeps its mode. ApplyConfig() on a running driver dropped a new wake_timeout_us ; it is kept, as is the new loaded_channels .

Validation ¶ max22200::Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip; EnsureInitialized() and ApplyConfig() call it before any I/O, ConfigureChannel() calls ValidateChannel() . They return Error::InvalidArgument for: an enum holding a value that is not an enumerator, or the reserved pair mode 3; an RREF that is neither kNoRref nor 15 kΩ to 100 kΩ ( kNoRref passes: only the milliamp conversions need it); a wake timeout outside 2.5 ms to 10 s; a CDR code above 126 (127 is "LS on", the coil at full VM with no regulation, Table 4) or a VDR code above 100; CDR on the high side (the chip ignores HSnLS in CDR), or SRC, HFS or DPM on the high side; SRC at 50 kHz or above ("SRC mode is only available ... for switching frequencies less than 50kHz"); HHF in VDR (the HIT check is CDR only); a DPM field wider than its bits. The runtime checks that need the chip's state return ChannelsActive instead: a drive-mode or side change while a channel is on, a pair-mode change while one of the pair is on. Kconfig ¶ Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig shows MAX22200 solenoid driver when the driver is a component of the project ( Installation ); the menu is _config/Kconfig . The options reach the code only through inc/max22200_kconfig.hpp , never through a driver signature: max22200 :: Error StartFromMenuconfig ( MyPort & port ) { static max22200 :: MAX22200 < MyPort > chip ( port , max22200 :: KconfigDefaults ()); return chip . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } Option Default Config field CONFIG_MAX22200_VARIANT_PLAIN / CONFIG_MAX22200_VARIANT_A MAX22200 variant CONFIG_MAX22200_CLOCK_80KHZ n (100 kHz) clock CONFIG_MAX22200_RREF_OHM 0 (not given) rref_ohm The channel settings are not Kconfig options: set them in code. Without Kconfig (plain CMake, other platforms) KconfigDefaults() returns Config{} . Both cases are host tests. Next: Porting .

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the MAX22200 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: Enable, wake-up and disable times; SPI timing: Electrical Characteristics (tEN, tWU, tDIS, SPI); Figure 1, p. 10 ENABLE and the 0.5 ms to SPI ready: Enable Logic Input, p. 14 The programming procedure: Programming Procedure; Figure 6, p. 23 32-bit and 8-bit transfers and the command echo: Reading and Writing Operations of Registers; Figures 10 to 13, p. 30 Communication error detection: Communication Error Detection (COMF), p. 34 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, drives CMD high and ENABLE high, waits tEN, wakes the chip (bare ACTIVE writes until ACTIVE reads 1 with UVM clear, within Config::wake_timeout_us ), runs the programming procedure of Figure 6, then checks that STATUS, every CFG_CHn and CFG_DPM hold what it wrote and that every 32-bit write echoed its command. On a wake timeout ( Undervoltage , Timeout ) it leaves ENABLE high with every channel off; on any other failure it drives ENABLE low. Either way the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds, and sends nothing. No call starts or resets the chip as a side effect. ApplyConfig() before the start only stores the configuration. InvalidArgument , ChannelsActive and Unsupported mean nothing was sent. Every port failure propagates: a transfer as Error::Bus , a pin write as Error::Pin . A command byte is never sent unless CMD went high, and CMD is driven low after every command byte, whatever happened. A call sends only the transfers the datasheet needs; the read-backs are per call, Verify::ReadBack , with their cost in the doc comment. The start-up checks are unconditional. An ONCH write ( SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() , SetBridge() ) is 2 transfers, or 1 (the data byte alone) when the last access was an ONCH write without Verify::ReadBack and nothing has happened since: no other access, no failed transfer or pin write, no ENABLE change, no COMER in a fault byte (p25: the command stays in force until rewritten). Its STATUS[7:0] byte updates GetLastStatusByte() . After a read-back that differs, the driver's copy takes the value read, and the bits that differ are not trusted for the ChannelsActive check; a channel whose CFG_CH write failed or read back different accepts no write while a channel is on. The driver never sends a CDR current code of 127 (unregulated full on), a VDR code above 100, CDR on the high side, SRC, HFS or DPM on the high side, SRC at 50 kHz or above, HHF in VDR, RFU bits in a command, or non-zero bits in CFG_DPM[31:15]. HitTimeCode() and CurrentCode() never round into 255 or 127. A drive-mode or side change is refused while any channel the driver switched (or may have switched, after a failed write) is on; a pair-mode change while either channel of the pair is on. Every wait is bounded: EnsureInitialized() waits tEN, then wakes the chip for at most Config::wake_timeout_us (one tWU and one STATUS read every kWakePollUs ), at most kStartAttempts attempts. tEN and tDIS are waited in full after the pin write returns; a slow pin (an I/O expander) adds latency, never shortens them. CMD idles high: the driver drives it high before EnsureInitialized() touches the chip and back high after every data phase, the one-transfer ONCH write included, also when the transfer failed. No read hides a clear-on-read flag: every 32-bit STATUS read, the driver's own included, ORs OVT and UVM into a latch, and every FAULT read ORs the flags it clears ( GetLatchedFaults() , emptied only by ClearLatchedFaults() ; handbook KB-CPP-119). A restart does not empty it; the start-up does not keep the power-on UVM it clears, and a reply a floating SDO produces (all ones, 0xFF fault byte) is never latched. The start-up reads and clears FAULT, so faults latched before it (the chip may keep them across an ENABLE cycle) do not hold the FAULT pin; it reports them in GetStartupFaults() (handbook KB-CPP-058). A load-dependent diagnostic (open load, plunger movement, HIT current) is sent only for a channel that Config::loaded_channels declares (handbook KB-CPP-131); Validate() and ConfigureChannel() refuse it elsewhere. No public helper returns a sentinel: a conversion without the input it needs, or of a code that is not a value ( FullScaleUa() without RREF, HitTimeUs() of the continuous code), returns InvalidArgument (KB-CPP-126). A register field that holds no enumerator (CMxy = 3) is refused, never stored ( DecodePairMode() ). Config{} holds the reset values of STATUS and every CFG_CHn (p36, p38-39). The datasheet gives no reset values for CFG_DPM (p40-41): Config{}.dpm is 0, the value written at start-up, not a known reset state. Config{}.variant is Variant::Max22200 , correct on both parts (a selective clear is refused); declare Variant::Max22200A only when the BOM says it is fitted. A missing GpioSet() or DelayUs() , or a GpioSet() that returns void , is a compile error; a missing GpioRead() gives Error::Unsupported from ReadFaultPin() ; a missing Log() logs nothing. Deinitialize() leaves every channel off, ACTIVE = 0 and ENABLE low, even after a failed write. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay ( EnsureInitialized() for 3 ms or more). Separate objects share no state. docs.text: The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, drives CMD high and ENABLE high, waits tEN, wakes the chip (bare ACTIVE writes until ACTIVE reads 1 with UVM clear, within Config::wake_timeout_us ), runs the programming procedure of Figure 6, then checks that STATUS, every CFG_CHn and CFG_DPM hold what it wrote and that every 32-bit write echoed its command. On a wake timeout ( Undervoltage , Timeout ) it leaves ENABLE high with every channel off; on any other failure it drives ENABLE low. Either way the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds, and sends nothing. No call starts or resets the chip as a side effect. ApplyConfig() before the start only stores the configuration. InvalidArgument , ChannelsActive and Unsupported mean nothing was sent. Every port failure propagates: a transfer as Error::Bus , a pin write as Error::Pin . A command byte is never sent unless CMD went high, and CMD is driven low after every command byte, whatever happened. A call sends only the transfers the datasheet needs; the read-backs are per call, Verify::ReadBack , with their cost in the doc comment. The start-up checks are unconditional. An ONCH write ( SetChannelsOn() , SetChannel() , SetBridge() ) is 2 transfers, or 1 (the data byte alone) when the last access was an ONCH write without Verify::ReadBack and nothing has happened since: no other access, no failed transfer or pin write, no ENABLE change, no COMER in a fault byte (p25: the command stays in force until rewritten). Its STATUS[7:0] byte updates GetLastStatusByte() . After a read-back that differs, the driver's copy takes the value read, and the bits that differ are not trusted for the ChannelsActive check; a channel whose CFG_CH write failed or read back different accepts no write while a channel is on. The driver never sends a CDR current code of 127 (unregulated full on), a VDR code above 100, CDR on the high side, SRC, HFS or DPM on the high side, SRC at 50 kHz or above, HHF in VDR, RFU bits in a command, or non-zero bits in CFG_DPM[31:15]. HitTimeCode() and CurrentCode() never round into 255 or 127. A drive-mode or side change is refused while any channel the driver switched (or may have switched, after a failed write) is on; a pair-mode change while either channel of the pair is on. Every wait is bounded: EnsureInitialized() waits tEN, then wakes the chip for at most Config::wake_timeout_us (one tWU and one STATUS read every kWakePollUs ), at most kStartAttempts attempts. tEN and tDIS are waited in full after the pin write returns; a slow pin (an I/O expander) adds latency, never shortens them. CMD idles high: the driver drives it high before EnsureInitialized() touches the chip and back high after every data phase, the one-transfer ONCH write included, also when the transfer failed. No read hides a clear-on-read flag: every 32-bit STATUS read, the driver's own included, ORs OVT and UVM into a latch, and every FAULT read ORs the flags it clears ( GetLatchedFaults() , emptied only by ClearLatchedFaults() ; handbook KB-CPP-119). A load-dependent diagnostic (open load, plunger movement, HIT current) is sent only for a channel that Config::loaded_channels declares (handbook KB-CPP-131); Validate() and ConfigureChannel() refuse it elsewhere. No public helper returns a sentinel: a conversion without the input it needs, or of a code that is not a value ( FullScaleUa() without RREF, HitTimeUs() of the continuous code), returns InvalidArgument (KB-CPP-126). A register field that holds no enumerator (CMxy = 3) is refused, never stored ( DecodePairMode() ). Config{} holds the reset values of STATUS and every CFG_CHn (p36, p38-39). The datasheet gives no reset values for CFG_DPM (p40-41): Config{}.dpm is 0, the value written at start-up, not a known reset state. Config{}.variant is Variant::Max22200 , correct on both parts (a selective clear is refused); declare Variant::Max22200A only when the BOM says it is fitted. docs.text: Drive modes ¶ How the MAX22200 drives a load, and how each ChannelConfig field maps to it: HIT and HOLD, current or voltage regulation, the chopping frequency, the HIT time, the side, pairs and bridges, and plunger-movement detection. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: Full-scale current constant KFS and the CDR accuracy: Electrical Characteristics (KFS0, KFS1, ITRERR), p. 9 The HIT and HOLD sequence, and the TRIG and SPI triggers: Functional Description - Two Levels Drive Sequence for Solenoid Valves; Figures 2 and 3, p. 14 Oscillator and per-channel chopping frequency: Chopping Frequency (FREQM, FRQ_CFG_); Table 1, p. 16 Slew-rate control and the duty-cycle limits: Slew-Rate Controlled Mode (SRC); Min and Max Duty cycle, Table 2, p. 17 VDR duty-cycle codes: Voltage Drive Regulation (VDR); Table 3, p. 17 CDR current codes, IFS from RREF and the half full-scale bit: Current Drive Regulation (CDR); Table 4; Full-Scale Current Setting; Half Full-Scale Setting, p. 18 HIT excitation time: HIT Excitation Time (tHIT); Table 5, p. 19 High side, parallel pairs and full bridges: Supported Driver Configurations; Tables 6, 7 and 8, p. 20 Plunger-movement detection, thermal shutdown, UVLO and the HIT check: Detection of Plunger Movement (DPM); Thermal Shutdown (TSD); Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO); HIT Current Not Reached Flag (HHF), p. 22 CFG_CHn: Configuration Register Description (CFG_CH_); Table 11; Register Details, CFG_CH, p. 27 CFG_DPM: Detection of Plunger Movement Register Description (CFG_DPM); Figure 9, p. 29 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . HIT, then HOLD ¶ When a channel switches on (ONCH set, or its TRIG pin high with trigger_pin ), the chip drives the HIT level for the HIT time, then the HOLD level until the channel switches off (Figures 2 and 3). HIT pulls the plunger in; HOLD, normally much lower, keeps it there with less heat. The HOLD time is not programmable: it lasts as long as the channel is on. Field Register bits Meaning hit HIT[6:0] CDR: peak current code; VDR: duty cycle in percent hold HOLD[6:0] The same, for the HOLD phase. Can change on the fly: SetHoldCode() hit_time HIT_T[7:0] 0 = no HIT phase, 1 to 254 = steps of 40 chopping periods, 255 = HIT forever Current drive (CDR) ¶ DriveMode::Cdr , the reset value, regulates the peak current cycle by cycle with the chip's lossless current sense. Low side only. IFS comes from RREF ( Config::rref_ohm ): Code Peak current (Table 4) The driver 0 "HS switch on, LS switch off": no current Accepted: off 1 to 126 code / 128 x IFS CurrentCode() converts milliamps; CurrentUa() converts back 127 "HS switch off, LS switch on": the coil at full VM, no regulation Refused everywhere ( ValidateChannel() , SetHoldCode() ) // RREF = 15 kΩ: IFS = 1 A, one code = 1 A / 128 = 7.8125 mA (Table 4) static_assert ( max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 500 , 15000 , false ). value == 64 ); // 500 mA static_assert ( max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 984 , 15000 , false ). value == 126 ); // the highest regulated current static_assert ( max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 990 , 15000 , false ). error == Error :: InvalidArgument ); // would be 127 static_assert ( max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 3 , 15000 , false ). error == Error :: InvalidArgument ); // would be 0 static_assert ( max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 250 , 15000 , true ). value == 64 ); // HFS: IFS = 500 mA static_assert ( max22200 :: CurrentUa ( 64 , 15000 , false ). value == 500000 ); half_scale (HFS) halves IFS and doubles the on-resistance, for better accuracy below 0.5 A; pass the channel's HFS to CurrentCode() . The loop regulates the peak; the average current is lower by half the ripple, which falls as the chopping frequency rises ("Fixed-Frequency Current Control"). hit_current_check (HHF_EN) sets the channel's HHF flag when the HIT current is not reached by the end of the HIT time; CDR only. Voltage drive (VDR) ¶ DriveMode::Vdr outputs a PWM voltage whose duty cycle is the code, in percent (Table 3). The current follows from VM and the coil's resistance, so it drifts with both. Low or high side. Code Duty cycle 0 0 % 1 to δMIN - 1 δMIN (the chip raises it) δMIN to δMAX the code, in 1 % steps δMAX + 1 to 99 δMAX (the chip lowers it) 100 100 % δMIN and δMAX are 4 % and 96 %, 8 % and 92 % at fMAIN ( ChopDivider::Div1 ), 7 % and 93 % with SRC (Table 2, DutyLimitsOf() ). The chip clamps by itself, so the driver passes the code as it is: 0 % and 100 % stay reachable. Codes 101 to 127 mean 100 % as well; the driver refuses them so that every duty has one code. Chopping frequency ¶ The oscillator runs at 100 kHz or 80 kHz ( Config::clock , STATUS.FREQM, global); each channel divides it ( chop , FREQ_CFG, Table 1): chop 100 kHz 80 kHz Period Div4 (reset) 25 kHz 20 kHz 40 µs / 50 µs Div3 33.3 kHz 26.7 kHz 30 µs / 37.5 µs Div2 50 kHz 40 kHz 20 µs / 25 µs Div1 100 kHz 80 kHz 10 µs / 12.5 µs ChopPeriodNs() gives the period exactly. A higher frequency lowers the ripple and raises the switching losses. slew_rate_control (SRC) slows the edges to about 200 ns for lower emissions, doubles the OCP deglitch time, and is allowed only on the low side below 50 kHz: Div4 or Div3 at 100 kHz, Div4 to Div2 at 80 kHz ("Slew-Rate Controlled Mode (SRC)"; ValidateChannel() enforces it). The chopping frequency and SRC can change while the channel runs. HIT time ¶ tHIT = HIT_T x 40 / fCHOP (Table 5), so a step is 40 chopping periods: 1.6 ms at 25 kHz, 2 ms at 20 kHz (the datasheet's example: 0 to 508 ms). // One HIT_T step is 40 chopping periods (Table 5) static_assert ( max22200 :: HitTimeCode ( 30000 , MasterClock :: Khz100 , ChopDivider :: Div4 ). value == 19 ); static_assert ( max22200 :: HitTimeUs ( 19 , MasterClock :: Khz100 , ChopDivider :: Div4 ). value == 30400 ); static_assert ( max22200 :: HitTimeUs ( 100 , MasterClock :: Khz100 , ChopDivider :: Div3 ). value == 120000 ); // exact static_assert ( max22200 :: HitTimeUs ( 254 , MasterClock :: Khz80 , ChopDivider :: Div4 ). value == 508000 ); // 20 kHz static_assert ( max22200 :: HitTimeCode ( 408000 , MasterClock :: Khz100 , ChopDivider :: Div4 ). error == Error :: InvalidArgument ); // beyond 254 steps: never rounded to 255 (forever) static_assert ( max22200 :: HitTimeUs ( 255 , MasterClock :: Khz100 , ChopDivider :: Div4 ). error == Error :: InvalidArgument ); // 255 is continuous: not a time HitTimeCode() never returns 255: a time beyond 254 steps is refused, because 255 is a HIT phase that never ends, which a rounding must not produce. Ask for it with kHitTimeContinuous . A non-zero time below half a step becomes 1, never 0 ("no HIT"). Low side and high side ¶ Side::Low (the reset value) is a load from OUTn to VM; Side::High a load from OUTn to ground. The high side runs VDR only and has no SRC, HFS or DPM ("Low-Side/High-Side Operations (HSnLS)"); ValidateChannel() refuses each. With VDRnCDR = 0 the chip ignores HSnLS altogether, so CDR on the high side is refused too. Pairs: parallel and full bridge ¶ Channels 0-1, 2-3, 4-5 and 6-7 form pairs ( Config::pairs , STATUS.CMxy). The chip takes a pair mode only while both channels of the pair are off; the driver returns ChannelsActive otherwise. Parallel ( PairMode::Parallel ): OUTx and OUTy tied together for twice the current; the lower channel's CFG_CH drives both, the upper one's is ignored. Table 6 says SPI drives the pair "both ONCHx and ONCHy set logic high"; the register description names only the lower ONCH. The driver switches both bits together, which satisfies both readings: SetChannel() on either channel switches the pair, and SetChannelsOn() refuses a mask that splits it. Full bridge ( PairMode::FullBridge ): an H-bridge for a latching valve or a brushed DC motor. ONCHy and ONCHx choose the state (Table 7), set with SetBridge() : BridgeState ONCHy, ONCHx OUTx OUTy HiZ 0, 0 Hi-Z Hi-Z Forward 0, 1 VM regulated with CFG_CHy Reverse 1, 0 regulated with CFG_CHx VM Brake 1, 1 ground ground HSnLS is ignored in a bridge. The register description of CMxy says "PWM regulation control on LS according to" the lower channel's CFG, while Table 7 takes Forward from CFG_CHy and Reverse from CFG_CHx; the driver writes whatever you configure for each channel and follows Table 7 in its documentation ( Status and limitations ). In both modes the TRGnSPI bits of the two channels together decide SPI or TRIG control (Tables 6 and 8). Plunger-movement detection (DPM) ¶ A moving plunger makes the current dip during HIT (back EMF); a stuck one does not. With plunger_detect (DPM_EN, low side) the chip watches the current from ISTART until IHIT or the end of tHIT, and sets the channel's DPM flag when no dip deeper than the threshold and longer than the debounce time came (Figures 4 and 9). The settings are global ( Config::dpm , CFG_DPM, SetDpm() ): Field Code Value start DPM_ISTART, 0 to 127 code x IFS / 127 ( DpmCurrentCode(ma, rref, 127) ) threshold DPM_IPTH, 0 to 15 code x IFS / 127 ( DpmCurrentCode(ma, rref, 15) ) debounce DPM_TDEB, 0 to 15 code chopping periods ( DebounceUs() ) The DPM currents divide by 127, the CDR currents by 128 (the datasheet uses both). Set ISTART just below the current at which the dip is expected; the current above ISTART must rise slower than 700 mA/ms for the detection to work. The datasheet does not say whether HFS scales the DPM currents; DpmCurrentCode() uses the full-scale IFS. Diagnostics per channel ¶ Field Flag When open_load_detect (OL_EN) OLF A disconnected load, sensed while the channel is off (below 2 V low side, above VM - 2 V high side). Clears when the channel switches on or FAULT is read hit_current_check (HHF_EN) HHF CDR: IHIT not reached by the end of tHIT. Clears on a FAULT read or a new cycle plunger_detect (DPM_EN) DPM No valid dip during HIT always on OCP Over 1.1 A: the channel is switched off. It stays off until it is switched off and on again Read them with ReadFaults() and ClearFaults() ( API guide ).

docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated MAX22200, through the host port host_max22200_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/max22200_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest max22200_host_example ). ESP32 ¶ ESP-IDF applications that run the driver on an ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_max22200_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. docs.text: Hardware ¶ The MAX22200's pins, bus settings, timing and power, as the driver uses them. Everything here is from the datasheet; nothing on this page is verified on hardware with this driver yet ( Status and limitations ). Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: The two parts and how each clears the FAULT register: General Description; Ordering Information, p. 1 Supply, logic levels, on-resistance, OCP and open-load thresholds: Absolute Maximum Ratings; Electrical Characteristics, p. 7 Full-scale current constant KFS and the CDR accuracy: Electrical Characteristics (KFS0, KFS1, ITRERR), p. 9 Enable, wake-up and disable times; SPI timing: Electrical Characteristics (tEN, tWU, tDIS, SPI); Figure 1, p. 10 Pins, CMD, ENABLE, FAULT and the TRIG inputs: Pin Configuration; Pin Description, p. 12 Current rating and safe operating area: Applications Information; Current Rating; Figures 14 to 17, p. 42 The application diagram: Typical Application Circuits; Application Diagram, p. 44 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Parts ¶ Part FAULT register Driver setting MAX22200A Selective clear on read: a read clears only the flags whose SDI bit is high Config::variant = Variant::Max22200A MAX22200 Every read clears every flag; a fault that arrives during the read is lost Config::variant = Variant::Max22200 (the default) The two parts are otherwise the same ("Clearing the FAULT Register", Ordering Information). The chip cannot tell which it is, so the variant is configured; the datasheet recommends the MAX22200A for new designs. The default, Max22200 , is correct on both: it never asks for a selective clear, and ClearFaults() sends all ones. Declare Max22200A only when the bill of materials names it and a bench check shows a zero-SDI read leaves a latched flag set ( bench steps 5 and 11 ): a selective clear sent to a MAX22200 clears every flag. The selective clear's SDI byte order follows Figure 8 (LSB byte first), one constant ( reg::kFaultClearLsbByteFirst ), not verified on hardware . The eight VM pins are one supply: bypass them with two 0.1 µF ceramics, one at pins 12 and 13 and one at pins 28 and 29, plus 10 µF bulk. TRIGA switches the even channels and TRIGB the odd ones when a channel is set to its trigger pin ( trigger_pin ); the driver never drives them. SDO and FAULT are open drain: fit a pull-up to the MCU's logic supply. The pinout, the block diagram, the circuit and both tables are drawn from docs/hardware.yml . Inside the chip ¶ The Simplified Block Diagram: the SPI interface feeds the VDR/CDR control logic, which drives the eight half bridges and reads back their current sense and open-load detectors; the LDO, the charge pump, the oscillator and the current reference set up its supplies, clock and full-scale current. One chip drives every load the half bridges support: a high-side solenoid, a low-side solenoid, a latched valve as a full bridge, two outputs in parallel and a brushed DC motor. The diagram has no flyback diodes: when the low-side FET turns off, the high-side FET of the same half bridge turns on and the coil current decays through it (Fixed-Frequency Current Control). docs.text: Part FAULT register Driver setting MAX22200A Selective clear on read: a read clears only the flags whose SDI bit is high Config::variant = Variant::Max22200A MAX22200 Every read clears every flag; a fault that arrives during the read is lost Config::variant = Variant::Max22200 (the default) The two parts are otherwise the same ("Clearing the FAULT Register", Ordering Information). The chip cannot tell which it is, so the variant is configured; the datasheet recommends the MAX22200A for new designs. The default, Max22200 , is correct on both: it never asks for a selective clear, and ClearFaults() sends all ones. Declare Max22200A only when the bill of materials names it and a bench check shows a zero-SDI read leaves a latched flag set ( bench steps 5 and 11 ): a selective clear sent to a MAX22200 clears every flag. The selective clear's SDI byte order follows Figure 8 (LSB byte first), one constant ( reg::kFaultClearLsbByteFirst ), not verified on hardware .

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( max22200_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-max22200.git external/driver-max22200 git submodule update --init external/driver-max22200 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-max22200 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE max22200::max22200 ) max22200::max22200 is an alias of the max22200 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect MAX22200_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver MAX22200_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-max22200 -B build-max22200 cmake --install build-max22200 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( max22200 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE max22200::max22200 ) The target is max22200::max22200 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated max22200_version.h go to include/max22200/inc/ , the template implementation to include/max22200/src/max22200.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-max22200) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-max22200 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-max22200.git components/max22200 max22200 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml max22200 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : max22200 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-max22200.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES max22200 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/max22200_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into max22200_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = max22200 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build.
docs.title: Installation

docs.text: A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( max22200_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result .
docs.title: Requirements

docs.text: A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-max22200.git external/driver-max22200 git submodule update --init external/driver-max22200 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ).
docs.title: Get the source

docs.text: This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-max22200 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE max22200::max22200 ) max22200::max22200 is an alias of the max22200 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect MAX22200_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver MAX22200_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI )
docs.title: CMake (any MCU, any host)

docs.text: To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-max22200 -B build-max22200 cmake --install build-max22200 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( max22200 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE max22200::max22200 ) The target is max22200::max22200 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated max22200_version.h go to include/max22200/inc/ , the template implementation to include/max22200/src/max22200.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ).
docs.title: Installed package

docs.text: Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-max22200) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-max22200 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-max22200.git components/max22200 max22200 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml max22200 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : max22200 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-max22200.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES max22200 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then.
docs.title: ESP-IDF

docs.text: Layer File Role Settings cmake/max22200_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters
docs.title: How the build is organised

docs.text: The version is set once in the settings file and written into max22200_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = max22200 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0"
docs.title: Version

docs.text: Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Status and limitations ¶ What this driver has and has not been shown to do, so you can decide whether it is ready for your use. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: High side, parallel pairs and full bridges: Supported Driver Configurations; Tables 6, 7 and 8, p. 20 The SPI, the 8-bit accesses and the daisy chain: SPI Detailed Description; Figure 5, p. 23 FAULT and its two clear-on-read behaviours: Fault Register Description (FAULT); Table 12; Clearing the FAULT Register; Figure 8, p. 28 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Status ¶ Version 0.1.0, not released On hardware Not verified on hardware. No board has run this driver yet: run the bench steps below first Tested against A protocol model of both parts ( Testing and CI ), a fuzzer and the quality gates Assurance level high (Kokeb Labs handbook): not qualified for use in a safety function Parts MAX22200 and MAX22200A (datasheet 19-100531 Rev 1). One chip per driver object; no daisy chain Start-up and wake ¶ EnsureInitialized() follows the programming procedure of Figure 6 (p23-24): CMD high, ENABLE high, then tEN (0.5 ms, "Enable Logic Input", p14). CMD idles high because the Command Register is written with CMD high for the whole transfer and at the CSB rising edge (p25-26); a data phase lowers it only around its own transfer. tEN and tDIS are minimums: the driver waits them in full after its pin write returns. A port whose pins sit behind a slow I/O expander adds its own latency on top; it never shortens them. STATUS is read: step 1 of the procedure, which clears UVM, set at power-up, and releases FAULT (p23, p27; "FAULT is always asserted at power-up", p22). All ones with a 0xFF fault byte is NoDevice : nothing drives the open-drain SDO (p12). Wake loop, the procedure's "wake-up completed?" decision: write ACTIVE = 1 alone, wait tWU (2.5 ms, p10), read STATUS. Done when ACTIVE = 1 and UVM = 0. Otherwise wait to the next 10 ms poll and write ACTIVE again. The masks, pair modes and channels are written only after the wake, so a write the chip refuses while UVM is set ("must be cleared ... to enable operations", p27) costs only a retry. UVM clears once VM is above the UVLO threshold (p22), so how long this takes depends on the supply ramp, not on tWU: Config::wake_timeout_us (100 ms by default, up to 10 s) bounds it. At Config::wake_timeout_us with UVM still set: Undervoltage . With UVM clear and ACTIVE still 0: Timeout . In both cases the driver stays uninitialised, every channel off, and ENABLE is left high: ENABLE low disables the device (p14), and the next start would wait tEN and the wake again from the beginning. The application decides: retry EnsureInitialized() (it costs one more timeout), report a supply fault, or cycle VM, the only reset the chip has short of a POR (p22). COMER is armed after the wake: a write rejected during the wake may set it, and nothing says a STATUS read clears it (p36: "Read Only"), so the driver checks it only for the writes that follow. The masks, every CFG_CH, CFG_DPM and the ONCH state are written; STATUS is read back. FAULT is read with every SDI bit high, which clears every flag on both parts ("Clearing the FAULT Register", p28-29). The logic registers keep their content until a POR (p22), and ENABLE low is not a reset (p14), so faults from before the start (a host reset with the chip powered) would hold the FAULT pin and look new. They are reported by GetStartupFaults() and in GetLatchedFaults() , and logged as a warning. Every CFG_CH and CFG_DPM is read back. A COMER raised by those writes ( CommunicationError ): ENABLE low for tDIS, high for tEN, and the whole procedure again, up to three attempts. If every attempt fails, cycle VM . Transfers: 48 when the chip wakes at the first poll, 4 more for each extra poll (a poke is 2, a STATUS read 2). Datasheet rules the driver applies ¶ Each has a test. CDR currents divide by 2^7 = 128 (Table 4): IHIT = HIT / 2^7 x IFS. CurrentCode() and CurrentUa() use 128. CFG_DPM's ISTART and IPTH divide by 127; DpmCurrentCode() uses that. Code 127 is not a current. Table 4: code 127 is "HS switch off, LS switch on", the coil at full VM with no regulation. The driver never sends 127 in CDR ( kMaxCdrCode = 126), and CurrentCode() refuses a current that would round to it. HIT times are exact. Table 5: tHIT = HIT_T x 40 / fCHOP, with fCHOP = fMAIN / 4, 3, 2 or 1 (Table 1). HitTimeUs() and HitTimeCode() compute with 40 x divider / fMAIN, so 33.3 kHz and 26.7 kHz are not rounded. HIT_T = 255 is "continuous IHIT" (Table 5), never the result of a rounding: HitTimeCode() refuses a time above 254 steps, and 255 is asked for by name ( kHitTimeContinuous ). HitTimeUs() refuses 255: it has no time. COMER is one bit of the fault byte. The flow chart's "STATUS<7:0> = 0x04" is the COMER bit (Figure 6); at power-up UVM is set too (0x06), so the driver tests the bit, never the byte. The selective FAULT clear's byte order. Figure 8 draws the SDI bit that clears OCP[4] in the fourth byte, the position of FAULT[31:24] in an LSB-byte-first transfer, as for a write (Figure 10). The driver sends the mask that way. This is a reading of a figure, not verified on hardware ; the order is one constant, reg::kFaultClearLsbByteFirst , with tests for both, and bench step 5 decides. An all-ones clear works in either order. The two parts clear FAULT differently and cannot be told apart over SPI ("Clearing the FAULT Register", Ordering Information). The default is Variant::Max22200 , correct on both parts: it never asks for a selective clear, and ClearFaults() sends all ones. Declare Variant::Max22200A only when the bill of materials names the A part and bench step 5 shows a zero-SDI read leaves a latched flag set; then ReadFaults() keeps the flags. A selective clear on the MAX22200, which cannot do one, is Unsupported . 0 % and 100 % duty are reachable in VDR. Table 3 makes code 0 a 0 % duty and 100 a 100 % duty, and the chip clamps the codes in between to δMIN..δMAX by itself (Table 2). The driver sends the code as asked. SRC only below 50 kHz ("SRC mode is only available ... for switching frequencies less than 50kHz"; Table 2 has no SRC row at 50 kHz). ValidateChannel() refuses SRC at 50 kHz and above. What the high side and VDR cannot do. With VDRnCDR = 0 the chip ignores HSnLS, and SRC, HFS and DPM are low side only ("Low-Side/High-Side Operations"); the HIT check is CDR only. ValidateChannel() refuses each. No configuration before the wake. Figure 6 loops until the wake-up has completed, and step 4 requires UVM cleared; the driver returns Undervoltage or Timeout instead of going on ( Start-up ). Mode and pair changes only with the channels off. VDRnCDR and HSnLS change only with every channel off (step 5c), CMxy only with both channels of the pair off (Register Details); the chip silently keeps the old value. The driver refuses them ( ChannelsActive ) and reports an ignored one with Verify::ReadBack . A parallel pair switches with both ONCH bits. Table 6: SPI drives a parallel pair with "both ONCHx and ONCHy set logic high". The driver switches both, and SetBridge() refuses a pair that is not a full bridge. Shutdown reports its writes. Deinitialize() reports the STATUS write that switches the channels off and clears ACTIVE, and still drives ENABLE low. DPM settings out of range are refused (an IPTH above 15), never clamped: DpmCurrentCode() and SetDpm() . CFG_DPM is compared on bits 14:0 only. Bits 31:15 are reserved, three of them read only with no reset value (p40-41); a full compare would fail on a real chip. No read hides a flag. A STATUS read clears OVT and UVM ("Read Clears All", Register Details) and a FAULT read on the MAX22200 clears every flag, whoever makes the read. Every such read, the driver's own read-backs included, feeds the latch of GetLatchedFaults() . The SPI requirements are values, not prose: mode 0, MSB first, tCLK, tCSPW, tCSS, tCSH and tCMS are constexpr and the ports check them with static_assert ( Porting ). Load diagnostics only on declared loads. Open-load, plunger and HIT-current detection report a missing load as a fault (OLF, DPM, HHF) and pull the shared FAULT pin. Config::loaded_channels declares the loads, and a diagnostic on any other channel is refused ( InvalidArgument ). Where the datasheet contradicts itself or is silent ¶ Which CFG regulates a full bridge. Table 7 takes Forward from CFG_CHy and Reverse from CFG_CHx; the CMxy description says "PWM regulation control on LS according to" the lower channel's CFG. The driver writes what you configure for both channels; bench step 6 below decides. Parallel pair ONCH. Table 6 says both ONCH bits; the CMxy description names only the lower channel's. Setting both satisfies either reading. What clears COMER. STATUS marks COMER "Read Only" (p36), unlike OVT and UVM ("Read Clears All"); nothing says a STATUS read clears it. The driver assumes the worst: it records COMER from the first STATUS read of each start-up attempt and, if it is set when the wake ends, clears it with ENABLE low (or, if it stays, relies on the read-back of every register); only a 0 to 1 transition repeats the procedure, and between attempts ENABLE goes low for tDIS and high for tEN. On a running driver the first call that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 in any fault byte returns CommunicationError , and the writes since the last fault byte with COMER clear are in doubt (their ONCH bits count as on, ApplyConfig() writes their registers again). A COMER that stays set would hide every later miscount: the start-up clears one the wake left with ENABLE low (bounded tries; the model clears it so, a test covers a chip where only a power-on reset does), and while it is set on a running driver every switch-off is read back (2 more transfers each), so a miscounted switch-off is reported as CommunicationError or WriteMismatch and the copy takes what the chip holds. A miscounted switch-on or configuration write in that state is not seen without Verify::ReadBack . The model keeps COMER until ENABLE falls or a power-on reset, and a test covers the reading where a STATUS read clears it. Bench step 4 decides. Which write a COMER blames. The fault byte of an access shows the chip before that access's data (Figures 10 and 12), so a miscount shows from the next access on: the call that reports it may not be the one whose write was ignored. The driver cannot tell which of the writes since the last clean fault byte it was, and doubts them all. A power-on reset between two accesses. The driver sees a reset from the next fault byte with ACTIVE = 0; ACTIVE is never written 0 while it runs. Until then it cannot know, and a reset chip drives nothing (ACTIVE = 0, p26-27). A one-transfer switch to a reset chip gets no fault byte back (the chip forgot the command: SDO floats in the model); the driver then sends the command, whose fault byte shows the reset. A reset between a read's command byte and its data: if the data comes back all ones (SDO floating, as in the model), one more command byte tells a reset from a value; if a real chip clocks out something else there, that one read returns it as data and the next call reports the reset. What a real chip clocks out for a data phase with no command after a reset is not given; bench step 8 checks it. No CRC on SDO. The chip protects nothing it sends, so a persistently floating SDO (every fault byte 0xFF, no answer) goes unnoticed by an application that only writes: no write can see it. A periodic ReadFaults() shows it: every flag reads set (and on a part declared Variant::Max22200 , whose FAULT read clears, GetLatchedFaults().lost is set too). Flags that come and go between two accesses. The latch keeps the summary flags of every fault byte, so an OLF that a switch-on clears or an HHF that a new cycle clears is kept once any access has clocked it out. A flag that is set and cleared with no access in between is not seen by any SPI read; the FAULT pin is the only witness. CFG_DPM's reserved bits. Bits 31:15 "must be set at zero" (p29), but p40-41 mark bits 20, 19 and 17 read only and give no reset value for most of them, nor for DPM_ISTART, DPM_TDEB and DPM_IPTH. The driver writes 0 there and compares only bits 14:0; the model reads the read-only bits as 1. Config{}.dpm is 0 by choice, not a known reset state. The command after ENABLE low. Not stated. The driver sends the command again after any ENABLE change, so the one-transfer ONCH write never depends on it. Whether HFS scales the DPM currents. Not stated; DpmCurrentCode() uses the full-scale IFS. Whether an 8-bit STATUS read clears OVT and UVM. "Read Clears All" is stated for the register; an 8-bit read returns only STATUS[31:24]. The driver assumes it clears nothing, and cannot latch flags it does not receive; the model clears them on 32-bit reads only. Bench step 10 decides. SPI clock. The SPI rows of the Electrical Characteristics give tCLK 100 ns (10 MHz), and "SPI Detailed Description" says the interface "can operate up to 5MHz" next to the daisy chain. kMaxClockHz is 10 MHz for one chip; the SDO pull-up's RC can set a lower limit (note 2). Bench step 1 runs at the board's clock. The fault masks' position. "Protection Circuits" says STATUS[15:8]; Table 10 and the Register Map put them at STATUS[23:16], which the driver uses. Thermal shutdown is said to set "one flag bit in the Fault register"; OVT is in STATUS. An open-load flag on a channel that is switched on. Open-load faults clear "if the corresponding output is turned on": the detection works while the output is off. A self-test that switches a channel on and then expects OLF may see it cleared. What the driver cannot see ¶ A write the chip acknowledges and discards (a glitch on a shared bus) leaves the chip different from the driver's copy. The start-up reads every register back ( WriteMismatch ); on a running driver only Verify::ReadBack proves a write landed. After a read-back that differs, the driver's copy takes the value read (ONCH, CFG_CH, HOLD, STATUS, CFG_DPM), and the bits that differ stay untrusted: a channel whose CFG_CH write failed or read back different accepts no write while a channel is on. A lost ONCH write locks the drive mode. A lost switch leaves a channel on that the driver thinks is off; a later drive-mode change then keeps the old mode with the new codes (step 5c), as a TRIG pin held high does (a CDR code 126 under VDR is a 100 % duty). Where it matters, use Verify::ReadBack on switches and mode changes, or change modes only right after EnsureInitialized() . What the model cannot show ¶ The model is written from the datasheet, by the same reading as the driver. It cannot show: the SDI byte order of the selective clear (rule 6) and the command echo of a 32-bit write, which the start-up check relies on (Figure 10); what clears COMER (a STATUS read, ENABLE low, or only a power-on reset), and whether the command in force survives ENABLE low; how long a real supply takes to clear UVM, and whether the chip takes ACTIVE before it has (the tests run both readings: active_needs_uvm_clear ); what SDO carries for a data byte sent to a chip that lost its command in a reset; the analog side: currents, ripple, OCP and open-load thresholds, DPM detection on a real valve, thermal limits; electrical timing: tCMS, tCMH (no value given), the SDO rise time through the pull-up at your clock. Before you depend on it ¶ Run these on your board: Board powered: EnsureInitialized() returns Ok in 48 transfers or more (4 per extra wake poll; logic analyser on CSB, CMD high in the command bytes and back high after every data phase), ENABLE high, 3 ms or more after ENABLE rose. Power VM up slowly or late: the wake loop re-pokes ACTIVE until it reads 1; with VM held under the UVM threshold past Config::wake_timeout_us : Undervoltage , every channel off. Measure how long the wake takes on your supply and set Config::wake_timeout_us with a margin. VM off: NoDevice . SDI disconnected: DeviceIdMismatch . A 32-bit write's second SDO byte equals its command. SetChannelsOn(0x01, Verify::ReadBack) and SetChannelsOn(0x00, Verify::ReadBack) 1,000 times each: Ok , the load follows. Without read-back, alternate SetChannelsOn(0x01) and SetChannelsOn(0x00) : 2 transfers for the first, then 1 each (one CSB low period, CMD low during it and high after), and the load still follows. Write STATUS with a 3-byte transfer by hand (a miscounted write), then: the next fault byte shows COMER; note whether a STATUS read clears it, whether ENABLE low clears it, and that a start-up after it passes. Raise an OCP on channel 4 (short OUT4 through a fuse-protected load) and a DPM fault on channel 4, then ClearFaults(Faults{.overcurrent = 0x10}) : OCP[4] clears, DPM[4] stays (rule 6). On a MAX22200 the same read clears both. Also on a part declared Max22200A : a ReadFaults() (SDI all zero) must leave OCP[4] set. A latching valve on a full-bridge pair: Forward and Reverse each regulated as configured, to settle the Table 7 question; scope OUTx and OUTy. CDR at RREF = 15 kΩ: measure the peak current at codes 32, 64 and 126 (expect 250, 500 and 984 mA within the accuracy table); a HIT time of code 100 at 33.3 kHz measures 120 ms. Power-cycle VM while running (or pull VM below the POR level for a moment) with channel 0 on, then call SetFaultMask(GetConfig().fault_mask) : it returns DeviceReset , the logic analyser shows the command byte and no data phase after it, and the output stays off (ACTIVE = 0). Repeat with SetChannelsOn() twice before the dip, so the call after it is the one-transfer switch: record the byte SDO returns for it, and check that the driver sends the command and returns DeviceReset . Then EnsureInitialized() restores every channel's configuration with every channel off. Note whether the chip takes an ACTIVE write while UVM is still set. Faults from before the start: with a load declared on channel 0 ( Config::loaded_channels ) and open_load_detect on, start, disconnect the load, wait for OLF, then call Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() again without cycling VM: the FAULT pin is released after the start, and GetStartupFaults().open_load has bit 0. OVT and UVM in the latch: dip VM below UVLO for a moment (without a power-on reset), then call SetFaultMask(mask, Verify::ReadBack) : GetLatchedFaults().undervoltage is set. Note whether an 8-bit read ( ReadChannelsOn() ) after a second dip leaves UVM set for the next ReadStatus() . A flag the chip clears by itself: with open_load_detect on channel 2 and its load disconnected while it is off, wait for OLF, then SetChannel(2, true) and ReadFaults() : FAULT no longer shows OLF[2] (p21), and GetLatchedFaults().open_load is set. A write whose reply fails: pull SDO low through a resistor during the data phase of SetPairMode(0, PairMode::FullBridge) only if the port can report the failure; otherwise interrupt the port's transfer after the data has gone out. SetChannel(0, true) then returns Uncertain with no CSB activity, and SetChannel(1, false) switches both channels of pair 0 off. A FAULT read with SDI all zero on the fitted part: note whether it clears a latched OLF (a MAX22200 does, a MAX22200A does not), and declare Config::variant from the result and the bill of materials.

The flow chart's "STATUS<7:0> = 0x04" is the COMER bit (Figure 6); at power-up UVM is set too (0x06), so the driver tests the bit, never the byte. The selective FAULT clear's byte order. Figure 8 draws the SDI bit that clears OCP[4] in the fourth byte, the position of FAULT[31:24] in an LSB-byte-first transfer, as for a write (Figure 10). The driver sends the mask that way. This is a reading of a figure, not verified on hardware ; the order is one constant, reg::kFaultClearLsbByteFirst , with tests for both, and bench step 5 decides. An all-ones clear works in either order. The two parts clear FAULT differently and cannot be told apart over SPI ("Clearing the FAULT Register", Ordering Information). The default is Variant::Max22200 , correct on both parts: it never asks for a selective clear, and ClearFaults() sends all ones. Declare Variant::Max22200A only when the bill of materials names the A part and bench step 5 shows a zero-SDI read leaves a latched flag set; then ReadFaults() keeps the flags. A selective clear on the MAX22200, which cannot do one, is Unsupported . 0 % and 100 % duty are reachable in VDR. Table 3 makes code 0 a 0 % duty and 100 a 100 % duty, and the chip clamps the codes in between to δMIN..δMAX by itself (Table 2). The driver sends the code as asked. SRC only below 50 kHz ("SRC mode is only available ... for switching frequencies less than 50kHz"; Table 2 has no SRC row at 50 kHz). ValidateChannel() refuses SRC at 50 kHz and above. What the high side and VDR cannot do. With VDRnCDR = 0 the chip ignores HSnLS, and SRC, HFS and DPM are low side only ("Low-Side/High-Side Operations"); the HIT check is CDR only. ValidateChannel() refuses each. No configuration before the wake. Figure 6 loops until the wake-up has completed, and step 4 requires UVM cleared; the driver returns Undervoltage or Timeout instead of going on ( Start-up ). Mode and pair changes only with the channels off. VDRnCDR and HSnLS change only with every channel off (step 5c), CMxy only with both channels of the pair off (Register Details); the chip silently keeps the old value. The driver refuses them ( ChannelsActive ) and reports an ignored one with Verify::ReadBack . A parallel pair switches with both ONCH bits. Table 6: SPI drives a parallel pair with "both ONCHx and ONCHy set logic high". The driver switches both, and SetBridge() refuses a pair that is not a full bridge. Shutdown reports its writes. Deinitialize() reports the STATUS write that switches the channels off and clears ACTIVE, and still drives ENABLE low. DPM settings out of range are refused (an IPTH above 15), never clamped: DpmCurrentCode() and SetDpm() . CFG_DPM is compared on bits 14:0 only. Bits 31:15 are reserved, three of them read only with no reset value (p40-41); a full compare would fail on a real chip. No read hides a flag. A STATUS read clears OVT and UVM ("Read Clears All", Register Details) and a FAULT read on the MAX22200 clears every flag, whoever makes the read. Every such read, the driver's own read-backs included, feeds the latch of GetLatchedFaults() . The SPI requirements are values, not prose: mode 0, MSB first, tCLK, tCSPW, tCSS, tCSH and tCMS are constexpr and the ports check them with static_assert ( Porting ). Load diagnostics only on declared loads. Open-load, plunger and HIT-current detection report a missing load as a fault (OLF, DPM, HHF) and pull the shared FAULT pin. Config::loaded_channels declares the loads, and a diagnostic on any other channel is refused ( InvalidArgument ).
docs.title: Datasheet rules the driver applies

docs.text: Which CFG regulates a full bridge. Table 7 takes Forward from CFG_CHy and Reverse from CFG_CHx; the CMxy description says "PWM regulation control on LS according to" the lower channel's CFG. The driver writes what you configure for both channels; bench step 6 below decides. Parallel pair ONCH. Table 6 says both ONCH bits; the CMxy description names only the lower channel's. Setting both satisfies either reading. What clears COMER. STATUS marks COMER "Read Only" (p36), unlike OVT and UVM ("Read Clears All"); nothing says a STATUS read clears it. The driver assumes the worst: it records COMER from the first STATUS read of each start-up attempt and, if it is set when the wake ends, clears it with ENABLE low (or, if it stays, relies on the read-back of every register); only a 0 to 1 transition repeats the procedure, and between attempts ENABLE goes low for tDIS and high for tEN. On a running driver the first call that sees COMER go from 0 to 1 in any fault byte returns CommunicationError , and the writes since the last fault byte with COMER clear are in doubt (their ONCH bits count as on, ApplyConfig() writes their registers again). A COMER that stays set would hide every later miscount: the start-up clears one the wake left with ENABLE low (bounded tries; the model clears it so, a test covers a chip where only a power-on reset does), and while it is set on a running driver every switch-off is read back (2 more transfers each), so a miscounted switch-off is reported as CommunicationError or WriteMismatch and the copy takes what the chip holds. A miscounted switch-on or configuration write in that state is not seen without Verify::ReadBack . The model keeps COMER until ENABLE falls or a power-on reset, and a test covers the reading where a STATUS read clears it. Bench step 4 decides. Which write a COMER blames. The fault byte of an access shows the chip before that access's data (Figures 10 and 12), so a miscount shows from the next access on: the call that reports it may not be the one whose write was ignored. The driver cannot tell which of the writes since the last clean fault byte it was, and doubts them all. A power-on reset between two accesses. The driver sees a reset from the next fault byte with ACTIVE = 0; ACTIVE is never written 0 while it runs. Until then it cannot know, and a reset chip drives nothing (ACTIVE = 0, p26-27). A one-transfer switch to a reset chip gets no fault byte back (the chip forgot the command: SDO floats in the model); the driver then sends the command, whose fault byte shows the reset. A reset between a read's command byte and its data: if the data comes back all ones (SDO floating, as in the model), one more command byte tells a reset from a value; if a real chip clocks out something else there, that one read returns it as data and the next call reports the reset. What a real chip clocks out for a data phase with no command after a reset is not given; bench step 8 checks it. No CRC on SDO. The chip protects nothing it sends, so a persistently floating SDO (every fault byte 0xFF, no answer) goes unnoticed by an application that only writes: no write can see it. A periodic ReadFaults() shows it: every flag reads set (and on a part declared Variant::Max22200 , whose FAULT read clears, GetLatchedFaults().lost is set too). Flags that come and go between two accesses. The latch keeps the summary flags of every fault byte, so an OLF that a switch-on clears or an HHF that a new cycle clears is kept once any access has clocked it out. A flag that is set and cleared with no access in between is not seen by any SPI read; the FAULT pin is the only witness. CFG_DPM's reserved bits. Bits 31:15 "must be set at zero" (p29), but p40-41 mark bits 20, 19 and 17 read only and give no reset value for most of them, nor for DPM_ISTART, DPM_TDEB and DPM_IPTH. The driver writes 0 there and compares only bits 14:0; the model reads the read-only bits as 1. Config{}.dpm is 0 by choice, not a known reset state. The command after ENABLE low. Not stated. The driver sends the command again after any ENABLE change, so the one-transfer ONCH write never depends on it. Whether HFS scales the DPM currents. Not stated; DpmCurrentCode() uses the full-scale IFS. Whether an 8-bit STATUS read clears OVT and UVM. "Read Clears All" is stated for the register; an 8-bit read returns only STATUS[31:24]. The driver assumes it clears nothing, and cannot latch flags it does not receive; the model clears them on 32-bit reads only. Bench step 10 decides. SPI clock. The SPI rows of the Electrical Characteristics give tCLK 100 ns (10 MHz), and "SPI Detailed Description" says the interface "can operate up to 5MHz" next to the daisy chain. kMaxClockHz is 10 MHz for one chip; the SDO pull-up's RC can set a lower limit (note 2). Bench step 1 runs at the board's clock. The fault masks' position. "Protection Circuits" says STATUS[15:8]; Table 10 and the Register Map put them at STATUS[23:16], which the driver uses. Thermal shutdown is said to set "one flag bit in the Fault register"; OVT is in STATUS. An open-load flag on a channel that is switched on. Open-load faults clear "if the corresponding output is turned on": the detection works while the output is off. A self-test that switches a channel on and then expects OLF may see it cleared.
docs.title: Where the datasheet contradicts itself or is silent

docs.text: A write the chip acknowledges and discards (a glitch on a shared bus) leaves the chip different from the driver's copy. The start-up reads every register back ( WriteMismatch ); on a running driver only Verify::ReadBack proves a write landed. After a read-back that differs, the driver's copy takes the value read (ONCH, CFG_CH, HOLD, STATUS, CFG_DPM), and the bits that differ stay untrusted: a channel whose CFG_CH write failed or read back different accepts no write while a channel is on. A lost ONCH write locks the drive mode. A lost switch leaves a channel on that the driver thinks is off; a later drive-mode change then keeps the old mode with the new codes (step 5c), as a TRIG pin held high does (a CDR code 126 under VDR is a 100 % duty). Where it matters, use Verify::ReadBack on switches and mode changes, or change modes only right after EnsureInitialized() .
docs.title: What the driver cannot see

docs.text: The model is written from the datasheet, by the same reading as the driver. It cannot show: the SDI byte order of the selective clear (rule 6) and the command echo of a 32-bit write, which the start-up check relies on (Figure 10); what clears COMER (a STATUS read, ENABLE low, or only a power-on reset), and whether the command in force survives ENABLE low; how long a real supply takes to clear UVM, and whether the chip takes ACTIVE before it has (the tests run both readings: active_needs_uvm_clear ); what SDO carries for a data byte sent to a chip that lost its command in a reset; the analog side: currents, ripple, OCP and open-load thresholds, DPM detection on a real valve, thermal limits; electrical timing: tCMS, tCMH (no value given), the SDO rise time through the pull-up at your clock.
docs.title: What the model cannot show

docs.text: Run these on your board: Board powered: EnsureInitialized() returns Ok in 48 transfers or more (4 per extra wake poll; logic analyser on CSB, CMD high in the command bytes and back high after every data phase), ENABLE high, 3 ms or more after ENABLE rose. Power VM up slowly or late: the wake loop re-pokes ACTIVE until it reads 1; with VM held under the UVM threshold past Config::wake_timeout_us : Undervoltage , every channel off. Measure how long the wake takes on your supply and set Config::wake_timeout_us with a margin. VM off: NoDevice . SDI disconnected: DeviceIdMismatch . A 32-bit write's second SDO byte equals its command. SetChannelsOn(0x01, Verify::ReadBack) and SetChannelsOn(0x00, Verify::ReadBack) 1,000 times each: Ok , the load follows. Without read-back, alternate SetChannelsOn(0x01) and SetChannelsOn(0x00) : 2 transfers for the first, then 1 each (one CSB low period, CMD low during it and high after), and the load still follows. Write STATUS with a 3-byte transfer by hand (a miscounted write), then: the next fault byte shows COMER; note whether a STATUS read clears it, whether ENABLE low clears it, and that a start-up after it passes. Raise an OCP on channel 4 (short OUT4 through a fuse-protected load) and a DPM fault on channel 4, then ClearFaults(Faults{.overcurrent = 0x10}) : OCP[4] clears, DPM[4] stays (rule 6). On a MAX22200 the same read clears both. Also on a part declared Max22200A : a ReadFaults() (SDI all zero) must leave OCP[4] set. A latching valve on a full-bridge pair: Forward and Reverse each regulated as configured, to settle the Table 7 question; scope OUTx and OUTy. CDR at RREF = 15 kΩ: measure the peak current at codes 32, 64 and 126 (expect 250, 500 and 984 mA within the accuracy table); a HIT time of code 100 at 33.3 kHz measures 120 ms. Power-cycle VM while running (or pull VM below the POR level for a moment) with channel 0 on, then call SetFaultMask(GetConfig().fault_mask) : it returns DeviceReset , the logic analyser shows the command byte and no data phase after it, and the output stays off (ACTIVE = 0). Repeat with SetChannelsOn() twice before the dip, so the call after it is the one-transfer switch: record the byte SDO returns for it, and check that the driver sends the command and returns DeviceReset . Then EnsureInitialized() restores every channel's configuration with every channel off. Note whether the chip takes an ACTIVE write while UVM is still set. Faults from before the start: with a load declared on channel 0 ( Config::loaded_channels ) and open_load_detect on, start, disconnect the load, wait for OLF, then call Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() again without cycling VM: the FAULT pin is released after the start, and GetStartupFaults().open_load has bit 0. OVT and UVM in the latch: dip VM below UVLO for a moment (without a power-on reset), then call SetFaultMask(mask, Verify::ReadBack) : GetLatchedFaults().undervoltage is set. Note whether an 8-bit read ( ReadChannelsOn() ) after a second dip leaves UVM set for the next ReadStatus() . A flag the chip clears by itself: with open_load_detect on channel 2 and its load disconnected while it is off, wait for OLF, then SetChannel(2, true) and ReadFaults() : FAULT no longer shows OLF[2] (p21), and GetLatchedFaults().open_load is set. A write whose reply fails: pull SDO low through a resistor during the data phase of SetPairMode(0, PairMode::FullBridge) only if the port can report the failure; otherwise interrupt the port's transfer after the data has gone out. SetChannel(0, true) then returns Uncertain with no CSB activity, and SetChannel(1, false) switches both channels of pair 0 off. A FAULT read with SDI all zero on the fitted part: note whether it clears a latched OLF (a MAX22200 does, a MAX22200A does not), and declare Config::variant from the result and the bill of materials.
