docs.text: Platforms ¶ The driver is MCU-agnostic: inc/ and src/ contain no SDK, RTOS or vendor header. A platform is three optional pieces around it, and only examples/<platform>/ holds platform code. Piece Where What it is Port examples/<platform>/ The class that implements the bus hooks for that MCU or OS ( Porting ) Example examples/<platform>/ A program that runs the driver there, built by CI Build integration the root CMakeLists.txt How that platform's build system finds the driver What exists today ¶ Platform Port Example Build integration Built by CI Host (Linux, macOS, Windows) examples/host/host_max22200_port.hpp (simulated chip) examples/host/ Plain CMake yes, run as a test ESP32 (ESP-IDF) examples/esp32/main/esp32_max22200_port.hpp examples/esp32/ Root CMakeLists.txt under ESP_PLATFORM (component) yes STM32, RP2040, nRF, other MCUs write one ( Porting ) none yet Plain CMake no Plain CMake ( add_subdirectory() or find_package() , see Installation ) covers STM32, RP2040, nRF and host builds. The root CMakeLists.txt also covers ESP-IDF: under ESP_PLATFORM it registers the repository as a component (a repository scaffolded without the ESP32 platform adds that branch back from the template when it needs it). Zephyr modules, Arduino library manifests and PlatformIO manifests are added only when a product needs them, and an example is added only together with a CI job that builds it. Add a platform ¶ The add-port skill has the details per MCU. In short: Create examples/<platform>/ with the port ( <platform>_max22200_port.hpp ), a small example program and a README with the wiring and the expected output. The folder is self-contained: it carries its own port and builds on its own. Build it in CI: a job in .github/workflows/ that builds the example, needed by the CI gate . A platform that CI does not build is not added. If its build system cannot use the root CMakeLists.txt , add the smallest manifest it needs, and say why in the pull request. Never put platform code in inc/ or src/ . Add a row to the table above and a page section if the platform needs one.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: Enable, wake-up and disable times; SPI timing: Electrical Characteristics (tEN, tWU, tDIS, SPI); Figure 1, p. 10 Pins, CMD, ENABLE, FAULT and the TRIG inputs: Pin Configuration; Pin Description, p. 12 The SPI, the 8-bit accesses and the daisy chain: SPI Detailed Description; Figure 5, p. 23 The Command Register and the fault byte: Command Register Description (COMMAND); Table 9; Figure 7, p. 25 32-bit and 8-bit transfers and the command echo: Reading and Writing Operations of Registers; Figures 10 to 13, p. 30 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from max22200::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the max22200::SpiPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Hook Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus, CMD and ENABLE up on the first call, each pin at its idle level before it becomes an output (below); true at once afterwards bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept yes One full-duplex transfer of 1 or 4 bytes, both buffers given, CSB low for all of them and high after bool GpioSet(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal signal) noexcept yes Drive CtrlPin::Cmd or CtrlPin::Enable ; false when the pin could not be driven void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes Wait at least us microseconds: tEN (500 µs) and tWU (2500 µs) at start-up bool GpioRead(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal& signal) noexcept no Read CtrlPin::Fault : ACTIVE while the pin is low void Log(LogLevel level, const char* message) noexcept no One line per lifecycle event or failure; plain text, never a format string The required hooks are checked exactly by the SpiPort concept: each parameter must have exactly the type above and each hook must be noexcept and return bool . A Transfer() that takes a uint16_t length, or a GpioSet() without noexcept , is a compile error, not a silent conversion (handbook KB-CPP20-006). An optional hook that is declared with another signature ( void GpioRead(...) , DelayUs(uint16_t) ) is a compile error too, never ignored (KB-CPP20-007). Bus requirements ¶ What the chip needs from the bus is in max22200_spi_interface.hpp as constexpr values (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as the host and ESP32 ports do: Constant Value From kSpiMode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0) SPI Detailed Description, p23 kMsbFirst true Figure 1 kMaxClockHz 10 000 000 (tCLK 100 ns; the SDO pull-up may set less) Electrical Characteristics, SPI rows, p10 kMinCsHighNs 30 (tCSPW) the same kCsSetupNs 30 (tCSS) the same kCsHoldNs 30 (tCSH) the same kContinuousWord false: no limit on idle SCK time inside a transfer the chip counts clocks while CSB is low (p34) kCmdSetupNs 20 (tCMS); tCMH has no value Electrical Characteristics, Figure 1 kTransferBytes 1 and 4: the only lengths the driver asks for Figures 10 to 13 kSdoOpenDrain true: fit a pull-up on SDO Pin Description, p12 The port below checks its clock this way ( kClockHz ). Control pins and their idle levels ¶ The port drives each control output to its idle level before it enables the pin's output driver and before the first transfer (handbook KB-HW-018): set the level, then configure the pin as an output. Pin CtrlPin Polarity Idle level Why CMD Cmd active high: ACTIVE = high selects the Command Register high ( ACTIVE ) The Command Register is written with CMD high for the whole transfer and at the CSB rising edge (p25-26); only a data phase lowers it ENABLE Enable active high: ACTIVE = high wakes the chip low ( INACTIVE ) The chip sleeps, every output Hi-Z, until EnsureInitialized() raises it FAULT Fault open drain, active low: ACTIVE = low = a fault input with a pull-up Read only ( GpioRead() ) Timing ¶ The bus: SPI mode 0, MSB first, up to 10 MHz. The driver calls Transfer() once for the command byte (with CMD high) and once for the data (with CMD low), then drives CMD high again: CMD idles high between transactions, and your port's EnsureInitialized() should leave it high. Never more than 4 bytes, so a polling transfer is fine. CSB must go high between the two. GpioSet(CtrlPin::Cmd, ...) must have taken effect before Transfer() starts (tCMS, 20 ns before the CSB falling edge, Figure 1) and CMD must still be high when CSB rises (p26), then for tCMH, for which the datasheet gives no value: a GPIO write that returns after the pin changed, before and after Transfer() , does both. A board that ties ENABLE high returns true for CtrlPin::Enable and does nothing. tEN and tDIS are minimum waits: the driver calls DelayUs() for them after GpioSet() returns. A pin behind a slow I/O expander adds its latency on top and never shortens them; it does stretch every CMD toggle, so put CMD on an MCU pin where you can. The port moves raw bytes: it never retries, never interprets the data and never configures the chip. The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public max22200 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // The bus settings platform_spi_init() uses, checked against the driver's requirements. static constexpr uint32_t kClockHz = 1'000'000 ; static_assert ( kClockHz <= max22200 :: kMaxClockHz , "above the MAX22200's tCLK limit" ); static_assert ( max22200 :: kSpiMode == 0 && max22200 :: kMsbFirst , "set the bus to mode 0, MSB first" ); // Bring the bus up once, CMD at its idle level high and ENABLE low before either pin becomes an // output; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One transfer: 1 byte (command or 8-bit data) or 4 bytes (32-bit data), CSB low throughout. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // CMD and ENABLE are both active high. Return false when the pin could not be driven. bool GpioSet ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool high = signal == max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; switch ( pin ) { case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Cmd : return platform_gpio_write ( kCmdGpio , high ); case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Enable : return platform_gpio_write ( kEnableGpio , high ); // tied high on the board? return true case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Fault : // an input: never driven default : break ; } return false ; } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: tEN (0.5 ms) and tWU (2.5 ms) at start-up. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : static constexpr int kCmdGpio = 5 ; static constexpr int kEnableGpio = 6 ; bool ready_ = false ; }; Optional hooks ¶ A port with every hook, as the ESP32 example has: class FullPort : public max22200 :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } bool GpioSet ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool high = signal == max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; if ( pin == max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Cmd ) { return platform_gpio_write ( kCmdGpio , high ); } return pin == max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Enable && platform_gpio_write ( kEnableGpio , high ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: the FAULT pin, open drain and active low. ACTIVE means a fault, a low level. bool GpioRead ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool high = true ; if ( pin != max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Fault || ! platform_gpio_read ( kFaultGpio , high )) { return false ; } signal = high ? max22200 :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE : max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; return true ; } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( max22200 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > max22200 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kCmdGpio = 5 ; static constexpr int kEnableGpio = 6 ; static constexpr int kFaultGpio = 7 ; }; With GpioRead() , ReadFaultPin() reads the FAULT pin without SPI; without it, it returns Unsupported . A use: // In the FAULT interrupt's deferred handler (never in the ISR: it uses the bus). max22200 :: Result < max22200 :: Faults > OnFaultPin ( max22200 :: MAX22200 < FullPort >& chip ) { const auto pin = chip . ReadFaultPin (); // no SPI if ( ! pin || ! pin . value ) { return max22200 :: Result < max22200 :: Faults >:: Failure ( pin . error ); } return chip . ReadFaults (); // which channel, which fault; the MAX22200A keeps the flags } A GpioSet() that returns void , or none at all, is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write, and CMD is part of the protocol. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error too. The compile-fail tests check each rule. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_max22200_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_max22200_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that CMD, ENABLE, SDI and SDO work: every 32-bit write echoed its command and every register read back what was written. NoDevice means SDO reads 0xFF (no supply, ENABLE low, no pull-up); DeviceIdMismatch means the chip did not take or echo the commands (SDI, CMD or CSB). With a load on channel 0: SetChannel(0, true, Verify::ReadBack) returns Ok , the load is energised, and ReadFaults() shows no OLF for channel 0 while it is on. Not verified on hardware with this driver yet. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract . Editor setup ¶ The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. docs.text: Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: Enable, wake-up and disable times; SPI timing: Electrical Characteristics (tEN, tWU, tDIS, SPI); Figure 1, p. 10 Pins, CMD, ENABLE, FAULT and the TRIG inputs: Pin Configuration; Pin Description, p. 12 The SPI, the 8-bit accesses and the daisy chain: SPI Detailed Description; Figure 5, p. 23 The Command Register and the fault byte: Command Register Description (COMMAND); Table 9; Figure 7, p. 25 32-bit and 8-bit transfers and the command echo: Reading and Writing Operations of Registers; Figures 10 to 13, p. 30 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from max22200::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the max22200::SpiPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use.
docs.title: Porting

docs.text: Hook Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus, CMD and ENABLE up on the first call, each pin at its idle level before it becomes an output (below); true at once afterwards bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept yes One full-duplex transfer of 1 or 4 bytes, both buffers given, CSB low for all of them and high after bool GpioSet(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal signal) noexcept yes Drive CtrlPin::Cmd or CtrlPin::Enable ; false when the pin could not be driven void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes Wait at least us microseconds: tEN (500 µs) and tWU (2500 µs) at start-up bool GpioRead(CtrlPin pin, GpioSignal& signal) noexcept no Read CtrlPin::Fault : ACTIVE while the pin is low void Log(LogLevel level, const char* message) noexcept no One line per lifecycle event or failure; plain text, never a format string The required hooks are checked exactly by the SpiPort concept: each parameter must have exactly the type above and each hook must be noexcept and return bool . A Transfer() that takes a uint16_t length, or a GpioSet() without noexcept , is a compile error, not a silent conversion (handbook KB-CPP20-006). An optional hook that is declared with another signature ( void GpioRead(...) , DelayUs(uint16_t) ) is a compile error too, never ignored (KB-CPP20-007).
docs.title: What you implement

docs.text: What the chip needs from the bus is in max22200_spi_interface.hpp as constexpr values (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as the host and ESP32 ports do: Constant Value From kSpiMode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0) SPI Detailed Description, p23 kMsbFirst true Figure 1 kMaxClockHz 10 000 000 (tCLK 100 ns; the SDO pull-up may set less) Electrical Characteristics, SPI rows, p10 kMinCsHighNs 30 (tCSPW) the same kCsSetupNs 30 (tCSS) the same kCsHoldNs 30 (tCSH) the same kContinuousWord false: no limit on idle SCK time inside a transfer the chip counts clocks while CSB is low (p34) kCmdSetupNs 20 (tCMS); tCMH has no value Electrical Characteristics, Figure 1 kTransferBytes 1 and 4: the only lengths the driver asks for Figures 10 to 13 kSdoOpenDrain true: fit a pull-up on SDO Pin Description, p12 The port below checks its clock this way ( kClockHz ).
docs.title: Bus requirements

docs.text: The port drives each control output to its idle level before it enables the pin's output driver and before the first transfer (handbook KB-HW-018): set the level, then configure the pin as an output. Pin CtrlPin Polarity Idle level Why CMD Cmd active high: ACTIVE = high selects the Command Register high ( ACTIVE ) The Command Register is written with CMD high for the whole transfer and at the CSB rising edge (p25-26); only a data phase lowers it ENABLE Enable active high: ACTIVE = high wakes the chip low ( INACTIVE ) The chip sleeps, every output Hi-Z, until EnsureInitialized() raises it FAULT Fault open drain, active low: ACTIVE = low = a fault input with a pull-up Read only ( GpioRead() )
docs.title: Control pins and their idle levels

docs.text: The bus: SPI mode 0, MSB first, up to 10 MHz. The driver calls Transfer() once for the command byte (with CMD high) and once for the data (with CMD low), then drives CMD high again: CMD idles high between transactions, and your port's EnsureInitialized() should leave it high. Never more than 4 bytes, so a polling transfer is fine. CSB must go high between the two. GpioSet(CtrlPin::Cmd, ...) must have taken effect before Transfer() starts (tCMS, 20 ns before the CSB falling edge, Figure 1) and CMD must still be high when CSB rises (p26), then for tCMH, for which the datasheet gives no value: a GPIO write that returns after the pin changed, before and after Transfer() , does both. A board that ties ENABLE high returns true for CtrlPin::Enable and does nothing. tEN and tDIS are minimum waits: the driver calls DelayUs() for them after GpioSet() returns. A pin behind a slow I/O expander adds its latency on top and never shortens them; it does stretch every CMD toggle, so put CMD on an MCU pin where you can. The port moves raw bytes: it never retries, never interprets the data and never configures the chip.
docs.title: Timing

docs.text: my_port.hpp class MyPort : public max22200 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // The bus settings platform_spi_init() uses, checked against the driver's requirements. static constexpr uint32_t kClockHz = 1'000'000 ; static_assert ( kClockHz <= max22200 :: kMaxClockHz , "above the MAX22200's tCLK limit" ); static_assert ( max22200 :: kSpiMode == 0 && max22200 :: kMsbFirst , "set the bus to mode 0, MSB first" ); // Bring the bus up once, CMD at its idle level high and ENABLE low before either pin becomes an // output; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One transfer: 1 byte (command or 8-bit data) or 4 bytes (32-bit data), CSB low throughout. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // CMD and ENABLE are both active high. Return false when the pin could not be driven. bool GpioSet ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool high = signal == max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; switch ( pin ) { case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Cmd : return platform_gpio_write ( kCmdGpio , high ); case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Enable : return platform_gpio_write ( kEnableGpio , high ); // tied high on the board? return true case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Fault : // an input: never driven default : break ; } return false ; } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: tEN (0.5 ms) and tWU (2.5 ms) at start-up. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : static constexpr int kCmdGpio = 5 ; static constexpr int kEnableGpio = 6 ; bool ready_ = false ; };
docs.title: The port

docs.text: A port with every hook, as the ESP32 example has: class FullPort : public max22200 :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } bool GpioSet ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool high = signal == max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; if ( pin == max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Cmd ) { return platform_gpio_write ( kCmdGpio , high ); } return pin == max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Enable && platform_gpio_write ( kEnableGpio , high ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: the FAULT pin, open drain and active low. ACTIVE means a fault, a low level. bool GpioRead ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool high = true ; if ( pin != max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Fault || ! platform_gpio_read ( kFaultGpio , high )) { return false ; } signal = high ? max22200 :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE : max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; return true ; } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( max22200 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > max22200 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kCmdGpio = 5 ; static constexpr int kEnableGpio = 6 ; static constexpr int kFaultGpio = 7 ; }; With GpioRead() , ReadFaultPin() reads the FAULT pin without SPI; without it, it returns Unsupported . A use: // In the FAULT interrupt's deferred handler (never in the ISR: it uses the bus). max22200 :: Result < max22200 :: Faults > OnFaultPin ( max22200 :: MAX22200 < FullPort >& chip ) { const auto pin = chip . ReadFaultPin (); // no SPI if ( ! pin || ! pin . value ) { return max22200 :: Result < max22200 :: Faults >:: Failure ( pin . error ); } return chip . ReadFaults (); // which channel, which fault; the MAX22200A keeps the flags } A GpioSet() that returns void , or none at all, is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write, and CMD is part of the protocol. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error too. The compile-fail tests check each rule.
docs.title: Optional hooks

docs.text: Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_max22200_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_max22200_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target.

docs.text: Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that CMD, ENABLE, SDI and SDO work: every 32-bit write echoed its command and every register read back what was written. NoDevice means SDO reads 0xFF (no supply, ENABLE low, no pull-up); DeviceIdMismatch means the chip did not take or echo the commands (SDI, CMD or CSB). With a load on channel 0: SetChannel(0, true, Verify::ReadBack) returns Ok , the load is energised, and ReadFaults() shows no OLF for channel 0 while it is on. Not verified on hardware with this driver yet.
docs.title: Check your port

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Run the driver on your PC first, with no hardware; then open a valve from your MCU: wire the chip, write a small port class, call two driver functions. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: Pins, CMD, ENABLE, FAULT and the TRIG inputs: Pin Configuration; Pin Description, p. 12 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated MAX22200, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/max22200_host_example MAX22200 driver 0.1.0 on the host max22200: initialised HIT 500000 uA for 20800 us, HOLD 148437 uA ONCH 0x01, flags 0x00 faults on channels 0x00 The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU MAX22200 Notes SPI SCK SCK Mode 0, up to 10 MHz; 1 MHz for bring-up on jumper wires SPI MOSI SDI SPI MISO SDO Open drain: fit a pull-up (1 kΩ to 4.7 kΩ to the MCU's supply) GPIO (chip select) CSB Low for each transfer GPIO CMD High while the command byte is written GPIO ENABLE Or tie it high IREF 15 kΩ to ground: IFS = 1 A 24 V (4.5 V to 36 V) VM 0.1 µF at each VM pair, 10 µF bulk GND GND, EP Connect the valve from OUT0 to VM (low side). FAULT, TRIGA and TRIGB can stay unconnected for this example (TRIG has a pull-down). The Hardware page has the full pin list, the timing and the power. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the max22200::max22200 CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-max22200.git external/driver-max22200 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up, moves bytes and drives two pins. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public max22200 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // The bus settings platform_spi_init() uses, checked against the driver's requirements. static constexpr uint32_t kClockHz = 1'000'000 ; static_assert ( kClockHz <= max22200 :: kMaxClockHz , "above the MAX22200's tCLK limit" ); static_assert ( max22200 :: kSpiMode == 0 && max22200 :: kMsbFirst , "set the bus to mode 0, MSB first" ); // Bring the bus up once, CMD at its idle level high and ENABLE low before either pin becomes an // output; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One transfer: 1 byte (command or 8-bit data) or 4 bytes (32-bit data), CSB low throughout. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // CMD and ENABLE are both active high. Return false when the pin could not be driven. bool GpioSet ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool high = signal == max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; switch ( pin ) { case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Cmd : return platform_gpio_write ( kCmdGpio , high ); case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Enable : return platform_gpio_write ( kEnableGpio , high ); // tied high on the board? return true case max22200 :: CtrlPin :: Fault : // an input: never driven default : break ; } return false ; } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: tEN (0.5 ms) and tWU (2.5 ms) at start-up. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : static constexpr int kCmdGpio = 5 ; static constexpr int kEnableGpio = 6 ; bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the transfer rules. 4. Open the valve ¶ main.cpp #include "max22200.hpp" int open_valve_0 ( MyPort & port ) { max22200 :: Config cfg {}; cfg . rref_ohm = 15000 ; // IFS = 15k x 1 V / 15 kohm = 1 A max22200 :: ChannelConfig & v = cfg . channels [ 0 ]; v . hit = max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 600 , cfg . rref_ohm , false ). value ; // 600 mA peak to pull in v . hold = max22200 :: CurrentCode ( 200 , cfg . rref_ohm , false ). value ; // 200 mA to hold v . hit_time = max22200 :: HitTimeCode ( 30000 , cfg . clock , v . chop ). value ; // 30 ms of HIT static max22200 :: MAX22200 < MyPort > chip ( port , cfg ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = chip . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // ENABLE, Figure 6, read-back of every register return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // NoDevice, DeviceIdMismatch: check the wiring } if ( auto r = chip . SetChannel ( 0 , true ); ! r ) { // one 8-bit write: 2 transfers, then 1 per switch return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } return 0 ; // HIT for 30 ms, then HOLD until SetChannel(0, false) } What each step does: The Config declares RREF, so the driver can turn milliamps into the chip's codes: CurrentCode() gives 600 mA as code 77 (77/128 x 1 A) and refuses a current it cannot regulate; HitTimeCode() gives 30 ms at 25 kHz as 19 steps of 1.6 ms (30.4 ms). EnsureInitialized() drives ENABLE high, waits tEN, runs the datasheet's programming procedure (STATUS read, STATUS write with ACTIVE = 1, every CFG_CHn, CFG_DPM), waits tWU and reads every register back. SetChannel(0, true) is one 8-bit write of ONCH (2 transfers; the next switch is 1). The chip drives HIT for 30 ms, then HOLD, until SetChannel(0, false) . This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. It is not verified on hardware ( Status and limitations ). If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() or Transfer() returned false EnsureInitialized() returns NoDevice SDO reads 0xFF: VM, ENABLE, the SDO pull-up ( Troubleshooting ) EnsureInitialized() returns DeviceIdMismatch SDI, CMD or CSB do not reach the chip EnsureInitialized() returns Undervoltage VM is below about 4 V, or still rising The valve does not move IREF and RREF, the HIT current against the valve's pull-in current, ReadFaults() Next ¶ API guide : switching, HOLD on the fly, faults, errors. Drive modes : CDR and VDR, HIT and HOLD, bridges, DPM. Configuration : every Config field, Kconfig. Examples : the host example and the MCU examples.

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply , and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --public --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR (its entry sets the About: description and topics): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-max22200 # the plan: every setting that would change python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-max22200 --apply # settings, security, Actions, rulesets, labels Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md .

docs.text: gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --public --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in.
docs.title: 1. Create and scaffold

docs.text: From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR (its entry sets the About: description and topics): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-max22200 # the plan: every setting that would change python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-max22200 --apply # settings, security, Actions, rulesets, labels Run it without --apply first to see what changes.
docs.title: 2. Apply the org settings

docs.text: python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY
docs.title: 3. Create the labels

docs.text: After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check .
docs.title: 4. Require the gate

docs.text: Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md .
docs.title: 5. Wire it in

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a protocol model of the chip ( tests/mock_max22200.hpp ). The model is written from the datasheet on its own: it has its own register map with page numbers and does not include the driver's max22200_registers.hpp ; tests/test_model.cpp cross-checks the two maps at compile time. It runs the chip transfer by transfer: the Command Register written with CMD high and its fault byte, the command staying in force until rewritten (p25), 32-bit writes LSB byte first with the command echo, 32-bit reads MSB byte first, 8-bit accesses of bits 31:24 with the STATUS[7:0] byte of an 8-bit write, the clock-count rule of COMER (the first 32 clocks of a 32-bit write, then every 8), COMER kept until ENABLE falls or a power-on reset (the worst reading of "Read Only"; the other is an option), STATUS reads that clear OVT and UVM, FAULT reads that clear selectively (MAX22200A) or wholly (MAX22200), CFG_DPM's read-only reserved bits reading 1, VDRnCDR and HSnLS locked while a channel is on or a TRIG pin high, CMxy locked while the pair is on, OLF and HHF cleared when a channel switches on and HHF on a new cycle, an OCP channel kept off until its ONCH goes off and on again, tEN after ENABLE and tWU after ACTIVE, a power-on reset that restores every reset value and forgets the command, and ACTIVE refused while UVM is set or (the other reading) taken. The faults are the bus and board conditions the port contract allows or the datasheet names: SDO floating high, stuck low or noise; SDI not reaching the chip; a power-on reset; VM below UVLO, or still rising; miscounted writes; writes acknowledged and lost (a shared-bus glitch); a TRIG pin held high; channel faults; failed transfers (before and after the chip took them), lost and replaced transfers; failed pin writes. They build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang, as ISO C++20 ( CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF , -pedantic-errors , the C++20 deprecations as errors) with the standard library's bounds checks on. max22200_host_tests runs 168 test cases; with the Kconfig, version, install, Doxygen, host-example, compile-fail and fuzz-corpus tests CTest runs 23 tests. The strict-dialect header checks ( max22200_header_checks ) compile each public header alone, first in its own translation unit, and assert __cplusplus == 202002L : on GCC and Clang with the host tests, with Arm GCC in the Cortex-M build ( max22200_optimised_build ), and with the ESP-IDF toolchain through examples/esp32/main/max22200_cxx20_check.cpp , compiled at -std=c++20 -pedantic-errors whatever dialect ESP-IDF uses for the rest (handbook KB-CPP20-001). cmake -S . -B build -DMAX22200_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_max22200.cpp The lifecycle (no I/O before the start, the transfers of the start in Figure 6's order, tEN and tWU, the wake loop and its timeout, a retried start, shutdown and restart), Validate() and ValidateChannel() against each datasheet rule, switching with and without Verify::ReadBack , parallel pairs and full bridges, channel settings and the mode lock, HOLD on the fly, pair modes, masks and DPM, STATUS and DeviceReset , both FAULT clear behaviours (the selective clear's byte order), the FAULT pin, the encodings and every unit conversion tests/test_fast_path.cpp The one-transfer ONCH write and every way it is invalidated, the STATUS byte it returns, the driver's copy after each kind of read-back mismatch, COMER at start-up (already set, cleared on read, new), CFG_DPM's reserved bits tests/test_latch.cpp The latch of clear-on-read flags fed by every STATUS and FAULT read (a STATUS read-back keeps the OVT it clears), the faults latched before the start cleared and reported, the raw ReadRegister() , a CMxy of 3 refused, load diagnostics only on declared loads tests/test_reset.cpp What the chip changes on its own: a power-on reset caught from the fault byte by every call before any data phase (with ACTIVE refused or taken while UVM is set), the restart after it; OLF and HHF the chip clears latched from the fault byte; the OCP latch; a miscounted write reported by the next call, its bits in doubt and its register written again; a failed reply: pair modes and FREQM unknown, Uncertain , registers written again; clear-on-read flags lost tests/test_model.cpp The model's register map against the driver's, and the model's own rules (command persistence, the clock count, COMER, OLF/HHF on switch-on, HHF on a new cycle, the OCP latch, CFG_DPM's read-only bits, the power-on reset, ACTIVE with UVM set) tests/test_bus_faults.cpp Every transfer of every operation, EnsureInitialized() included, fails in turn, before and after the chip took it; each returns Bus , CMD is left low and the next call works. Every pin write fails in turn; each returns Pin and a command without CMD high is never sent tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( max22200_fuzz_max22200_corpus ), see below tests/test_errors.cpp Every chip-specific value (16 to 23) and Unsupported are returned by a real call tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header (also against a 9.8.7 probe) tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port without DelayUs() , without GpioSet() , with a void GpioSet() , a Transfer() with a narrower length or without noexcept , a DelayUs(uint16_t) , a void GpioRead() , a GpioRead() that takes the signal by value, a Log() with another signature, a class that is not a port tests/mock_max22200.hpp The chip model; the mock ports over it are in mock_max22200_bus.hpp tests/check_version_copy.cmake _config/Doxyfile carries the CMake version examples/host/ The host example, built with the test flags and run ( max22200_host_example ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(max22200) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed The model does not reproduce the chip's analog or electrical behaviour, and the points the datasheet leaves open are modelled one way and listed: see Status and limitations . Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver receives comes from SDO and from the port's return values, so that is what a noisy cable, an unplugged board or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_max22200.cpp lets libFuzzer choose the part and a configuration (sometimes for the other part, sometimes invalid), then up to 64 driver calls, and on every transfer what the bus does: pass the model's reply, fail the transfer (before or after the chip took it), lose it (the chip never sees it, SDO floats), flip bits of the reply or replace it; on every pin write whether it fails. Between calls it changes the board: SDO floating, stuck low or noisy, SDI not reaching the chip, a power-on reset, VM below UVLO, a miscounted or a lost write, a failed reply followed by a miscount of the next write, a TRIG pin held high, channel faults. After every call the target checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines (never one documented as not returned) and T{} ; every transfer is 1 or 4 bytes with both buffers, and a 4-byte transfer never has CMD high; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer or a pin write; InvalidArgument , ChannelsActive and Unsupported mean nothing was sent; a reset chip is never re-activated without a new start, under both readings of whether ACTIVE is taken while UVM is set; no switch-off is held back : after a SetChannelsOn() that returns Uncertain , each pair on the chip ends at the request or only loses bits, and every channel asked off that the driver could know was on is off; a SetChannel(ch, false) that returns Ok leaves the channel off. Both are checked while the bus delivered the call as sent and no write was lost unseen since the last start (a dropped write, deaf SDI, a TRIG pin high, a lost transfer: a successful start clears this). A miscount does not stop the checks: an earlier one the driver has not seen yet only narrows "could know" to its copy, and one armed for the call itself skips them for that call, except the SetChannel() check while detection is already degraded (every switch-off is then read back); a miscount the driver is blind to (SDO not carrying the chip's fault bytes while COMER is set) and a forged reply count as hidden state; a drive-mode change that returns Ok is in force : after a ConfigureChannel() that returns Ok on a bus that delivered it, the chip holds the requested drive mode and side (it takes them only with every channel off, 5c); CMD is high (its idle level) after every call that drove pins without a failure; ENABLE is low after a failed start that drove it (a wake timeout excepted) and after Deinitialize() ; the chip never holds a channel setting the driver would refuse (a CDR code of 127, CDR on the high side, a VDR code above 100) nor reserved bits, unless a transfer was lost while reported as done, a TRIG pin was held high, or the board dropped or miscounted a write (the chip then keeps a mode the driver cannot see); a lone ONCH data byte (the one-transfer write) goes out only while the chip's command in force is the 8-bit STATUS write, unless the board reset the chip, SDI was deaf or a transfer was lost since the last command; EnsureInitialized() never returns Ok on a dead bus (SDO floating or stuck, SDI not reaching the chip) unless a transfer of the call was tampered with; after it, tWU has passed; while every call since the start was trusted and the board did nothing behind the driver's back, the chip holds exactly what the driver says it wrote: ONCH, STATUS, every CFG_CHn and CFG_DPM. The fuzzer's first runs broke three promises. Two were promises stated too strongly (a call that drives no pin keeps CMD as an earlier failed pin write left it; a start that fails before it drives ENABLE leaves ENABLE as it was), kept as regress-cmd-left-high-by-earlier-pin-failure and regress-failed-bus-up-keeps-enable . The third, regress-trig-high-keeps-old-drive-mode , is a limit of the chip: with a TRIG pin high the chip keeps the old drive mode and takes the new codes, so a CDR code of 126 written with a change to VDR runs as a 100 % duty. The driver cannot see the TRIG pins; it is documented ( Hardware ), and Verify::ReadBack reports it. Reviewing the same path found that a failed ONCH write that reached the chip left the mode-change check blind to the channel it switched on; the driver now counts such channels as on (unit test "After a failed ONCH write ..."). After the second review's changes it broke two more. regress-garbage-readback-trusted : a read-back through a stuck-low SDO differed, the driver took the garbage as the chip's ONCH, and a later drive-mode change landed on a channel that was really on; now the bits that differ stay untrusted, and a channel whose CFG_CH write failed or read back different accepts no write while a channel is on. regress-lost-onch-write-locks-drive-mode : the board drops an ONCH write the driver believes, so a channel stays on and locks the drive mode, as a TRIG pin does; it is a board fault only a read-back can see, documented on Status and limitations . After the wake loop it broke one: regress-forged-wake-read , a STATUS read replaced on the bus showed ACTIVE before the chip had it, so the start finished less than tWU after ACTIVE rose. A transfer the port reports as good but the chip never saw is invisible to the driver; the promise excuses it, and every output is still off at that point. With the switch-off checks running through miscounts it broke one: regress-failed-readback-drops-doubt . While COMER stayed set, a switch-off was miscounted and its forced read-back failed; the driver then trusted the copy ("off"), and a later refused mask sent nothing while the channel still drove. A failed read-back now leaves the channels asked off in doubt (unit test "COMER: a degraded switch-off whose read-back fails stays in doubt"). CI's fuzzing then found regress-unverified-switch-off-held-back : a switch-off was miscounted, the next access's fault bytes were lost on the bus (0xFF), so the COMER went unseen, and a SetChannelsOn() refused with Uncertain skipped its write because the copy already matched, leaving the channel on. A switch-off that no clean fault byte has vouched for now counts as possibly on, so the mask goes out again (unit test "Off: a refused mask re-sends a switch-off no fault byte has vouched for"). A new board event, a failed reply followed by a miscount of the next write, and a new promise (a ConfigureChannel() that returns Ok changed the drive mode and side on the chip) found regress-miscounted-settling-write-1 to -4 : a write that settled the doubt a failed reply left was itself miscounted, and the doubt was lost (a switch-off held back, a switch-on in a pair of unknown mode, a drive-mode change ignored by the chip while a channel drove). The doubt a write settles now stays recorded until a clean fault byte or a read-back proves it, and a configuration write stops before its data at a new COMER (unit tests "COMER: doubt a miscounted settling write cleared comes back" and "COMER: a configuration write stops before its data at a new COMER"). Running on, it found regress-degraded-config-write-1 to -4 : with COMER already set, a miscounted CFG_CH write was trusted; ConfigureChannel() now reads back in that state (unit test "COMER: while degraded, ConfigureChannel reads back"). regress-blind-miscount-sdo-floating and regress-forged-reply-vouches-miscount were gaps in the promise, not the driver: with SDO floating the driver cannot see a COMER at all, and a reply forged on the bus can show a clean fault byte that vouches for a write the chip ignored (the chip sends no CRC). Both now count as hidden state until the next start. regress-deaf-sdi-loses-onch-write : SDI that does not reach the chip loses every write, an ONCH write too, so a channel stays on and locks the drive mode, as a dropped write does; the promise excuses it like the other board faults only a read-back can see. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM and its libc++) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DMAX22200_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DMAX22200_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_max22200 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_max22200 -max_total_time = 300 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_max22200 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_max22200 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_max22200/ on GCC and Clang: the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise ( regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request (job Host quality / fuzz ). A local run of 4 minutes (12.2 million runs) broke no promise; on macOS the libFuzzer build uses UBSan's recover mode with UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 and -fno-sanitize=function , because Apple's linker rejects that object otherwise (CI builds on Linux with the CMake flags). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high This driver (local) Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 highest 12 ( Validate() , ValidateChannel() ); 11 in the driver class ( initialize() ) Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 within the limit Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 within the limit Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % 94.6 % (846 of 894) Branch coverage same run at least 75 % 87.5 % (555 of 634) MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) measured in CI Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report clean locally (Apple Clang) Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise clean locally (4 minutes, 12.2 million runs) The local figures are GCC 15 and gcovr 8.7 with the CI's options; CI uses GCC 14. The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DMAX22200_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DMAX22200_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target max22200_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ Not verified on hardware. The ESP32 example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it switches channel 0 every half second and logs ONCH, the STATUS flags and the FAULT bytes. The steps to run before depending on the driver are on Status and limitations ; record the board and the result in the pull request's bench-status section.

A miscount does not stop the checks: an earlier one the driver has not seen yet only narrows "could know" to its copy, and one armed for the call itself skips them for that call, except the SetChannel() check while detection is already degraded (every switch-off is then read back); a miscount the driver is blind to (SDO not carrying the chip's fault bytes while COMER is set) and a forged reply count as hidden state; a drive-mode change that returns Ok is in force : after a ConfigureChannel() that returns Ok on a bus that delivered it, the chip holds the requested drive mode and side (it takes them only with every channel off, 5c); CMD is high (its idle level) after every call that drove pins without a failure; ENABLE is low after a failed start that drove it (a wake timeout excepted) and after Deinitialize() ; the chip never holds a channel setting the driver would refuse (a CDR code of 127, CDR on the high side, a VDR code above 100) nor reserved bits, unless a transfer was lost while reported as done, a TRIG pin was held high, or the board dropped or miscounted a write (the chip then keeps a mode the driver cannot see); a lone ONCH data byte (the one-transfer write) goes out only while the chip's command in force is the 8-bit STATUS write, unless the board reset the chip, SDI was deaf or a transfer was lost since the last command; EnsureInitialized() never returns Ok on a dead bus (SDO floating or stuck, SDI not reaching the chip) unless a transfer of the call was tampered with; after it, tWU has passed; while every call since the start was trusted and the board did nothing behind the driver's back, the chip holds exactly what the driver says it wrote: ONCH, STATUS, every CFG_CHn and CFG_DPM. The fuzzer's first runs broke three promises. Two were promises stated too strongly (a call that drives no pin keeps CMD as an earlier failed pin write left it; a start that fails before it drives ENABLE leaves ENABLE as it was), kept as regress-cmd-left-high-by-earlier-pin-failure and regress-failed-bus-up-keeps-enable . The third, regress-trig-high-keeps-old-drive-mode , is a limit of the chip: with a TRIG pin high the chip keeps the old drive mode and takes the new codes, so a CDR code of 126 written with a change to VDR runs as a 100 % duty. The driver cannot see the TRIG pins; it is documented ( Hardware ), and Verify::ReadBack reports it. Reviewing the same path found that a failed ONCH write that reached the chip left the mode-change check blind to the channel it switched on; the driver now counts such channels as on (unit test "After a failed ONCH write ..."). After the second review's changes it broke two more. regress-garbage-readback-trusted : a read-back through a stuck-low SDO differed, the driver took the garbage as the chip's ONCH, and a later drive-mode change landed on a channel that was really on; now the bits that differ stay untrusted, and a channel whose CFG_CH write failed or read back different accepts no write while a channel is on. regress-lost-onch-write-locks-drive-mode : the board drops an ONCH write the driver believes, so a channel stays on and locks the drive mode, as a TRIG pin does; it is a board fault only a read-back can see, documented on Status and limitations . After the wake loop it broke one: regress-forged-wake-read , a STATUS read replaced on the bus showed ACTIVE before the chip had it, so the start finished less than tWU after ACTIVE rose. A transfer the port reports as good but the chip never saw is invisible to the driver; the promise excuses it, and every output is still off at that point. With the switch-off checks running through miscounts it broke one: regress-failed-readback-drops-doubt . While COMER stayed set, a switch-off was miscounted and its forced read-back failed; the driver then trusted the copy ("off"), and a later refused mask sent nothing while the channel still drove. A failed read-back now leaves the channels asked off in doubt (unit test "COMER: a degraded switch-off whose read-back fails stays in doubt"). CI's fuzzing then found regress-unverified-switch-off-held-back : a switch-off was miscounted, the next access's fault bytes were lost on the bus (0xFF), so the COMER went unseen, and a SetChannelsOn() refused with Uncertain skipped its write because the copy already matched, leaving the channel on. A switch-off that no clean fault byte has vouched for now counts as possibly on, so the mask goes out again (unit test "Off: a refused mask re-sends a switch-off no fault byte has vouched for"). A new board event, a failed reply followed by a miscount of the next write, and a new promise (a ConfigureChannel() that returns Ok changed the drive mode and side on the chip) found regress-miscounted-settling-write-1 to -4 : a write that settled the doubt a failed reply left was itself miscounted, and the doubt was lost (a switch-off held back, a switch-on in a pair of unknown mode, a drive-mode change ignored by the chip while a channel drove). The doubt a write settles now stays recorded until a clean fault byte or a read-back proves it, and a configuration write stops before its data at a new COMER (unit tests "COMER: doubt a miscounted settling write cleared comes back" and "COMER: a configuration write stops before its data at a new COMER"). Running on, it found regress-degraded-config-write-1 to -4 : with COMER already set, a miscounted CFG_CH write was trusted; ConfigureChannel() now reads back in that state (unit test "COMER: while degraded, ConfigureChannel reads back"). regress-blind-miscount-sdo-floating and regress-forged-reply-vouches-miscount were gaps in the promise, not the driver: with SDO floating the driver cannot see a COMER at all, and a reply forged on the bus can show a clean fault byte that vouches for a write the chip ignored (the chip sends no CRC). Both now count as hidden state until the next start. regress-deaf-sdi-loses-onch-write : SDI that does not reach the chip loses every write, an ONCH write too, so a channel stays on and locks the drive mode, as a dropped write does; the promise excuses it like the other board faults only a read-back can see. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM and its libc++) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DMAX22200_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DMAX22200_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_max22200 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_max22200 -max_total_time = 300 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_max22200 The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_max22200 , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_max22200/ on GCC and Clang: the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise ( regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request (job Host quality / fuzz ). A local run of 4 minutes (12.2 million runs) broke no promise; on macOS the libFuzzer build uses UBSan's recover mode with UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 and -fno-sanitize=function , because Apple's linker rejects that object otherwise (CI builds on Linux with the CMake flags).

docs.text: The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high This driver (local) Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 highest 12 ( Validate() , ValidateChannel() ); 11 in the driver class ( initialize() ) Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 within the limit Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 within the limit Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % 94.6 % (846 of 894) Branch coverage same run at least 75 % 87.5 % (555 of 634) MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) measured in CI Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report clean locally (Apple Clang) Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise clean locally (4 minutes, 12.2 million runs) The local figures are GCC 15 and gcovr 8.7 with the CI's options; CI uses GCC 14. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. Hook the optional Log() up first: every failure logs one line. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices 19-100531 1: Overcurrent and open-load protection: Protection Circuits; Overcurrent Protection (OCP); Open-Load Detection (OL), p. 21 Plunger-movement detection, thermal shutdown, UVLO and the HIT check: Detection of Plunger Movement (DPM); Thermal Shutdown (TSD); Undervoltage Lockout (UVLO); HIT Current Not Reached Flag (HHF), p. 22 Communication error detection: Communication Error Detection (COMF), p. 34 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns Bus or Pin ¶ The port reported a failure: Bus from EnsureInitialized() or Transfer() , Pin from GpioSet() . Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the CMD and ENABLE pins in your port against the board; a board with ENABLE tied high still returns true for CtrlPin::Enable . With a logic analyser: ENABLE rises, then after 0.5 ms the first transfer, one byte 0x00 with CMD high. EnsureInitialized returns NoDevice ¶ STATUS read 0xFFFFFFFF with a 0xFF fault byte: nothing pulls SDO low. SDO is open drain, so a missing chip, an unpowered chip and a sleeping chip all read 0xFF through the pull-up. VM between 4.5 V and 36 V at the chip, and V18 at 1.8 V (the chip makes its own logic supply from VM). ENABLE high at the pin (above 0.9 V) when the first transfer starts. SDO wired to MISO, and CSB going low for each transfer. EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch ¶ The chip did not answer as a MAX22200 does: a 32-bit write did not echo its command byte (Figure 10), or STATUS read back after the wake-up does not hold what was written (ACTIVE set, every writable bit as sent). SDO stuck low (reads 0x00): a short, or a pull-up too strong for the chip to pull down. SDI not reaching the chip: the chip keeps taking 0x00 (a STATUS read) and never sees a write. CMD not reaching the chip, or changing too late: the command byte is taken as data. CMD must be high before the transfer starts and at the CSB rising edge. SPI mode: mode 0 only (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0), MSB first. A slow SDO edge: lower the clock to 1 MHz, use a stronger pull-up (1 kΩ). EnsureInitialized returns WriteMismatch ¶ A CFG_CHn or CFG_DPM register read back differs from what was written: the chip ignored or lost a write. On a bus shared with other chips a lost frame does this; the driver reports it instead of starting with an unprogrammed channel. Retry EnsureInitialized() ; if it persists, check the chip select of the other devices (only one low at a time). EnsureInitialized returns Undervoltage ¶ UVM was still set when Config::wake_timeout_us (100 ms by default) ran out, with ACTIVE written again every kWakePollUs : VM is below the UVLO threshold (4 V typ), keeps dipping, or rises slowly. The driver is uninitialised, every channel off, ENABLE left high. Measure VM at the chip during the start; for a slow supply raise Config::wake_timeout_us (up to 10 s) or call EnsureInitialized() again later. ENABLE low is not a reset (p14): if UVM persists with VM in range, cycle VM, which ends in a power-on reset (p22). EnsureInitialized returns Timeout ¶ UVM read clear but ACTIVE never read 1 within Config::wake_timeout_us , although ACTIVE was written again every kWakePollUs . The chip is not accepting writes: check SDI and CMD (CMD left low turns commands into data), then cycle VM. EnsureInitialized returns CommunicationError ¶ Every attempt saw COMER go from 0 to 1: the chip counted a number of clocks other than 8 or 32 in a write and ignored it ("Communication Error Detection (COMF)"). Check that CSB stays low for exactly the 1 or 4 bytes of a transfer (no gap that releases it, no extra byte), and SCK for glitches. A setter returns ChannelsActive ¶ The chip changes the drive mode or the side only with every channel off, and a pair mode only with both channels of the pair off (Programming Procedure, step 5c; Register Details). Switch them off with SetChannelsOn() first. After a failed ONCH write the channels it would have switched count as on until a write succeeds: SetChannelsOn(GetChannelsOn()) settles it. ReadBack returns WriteMismatch for a drive-mode change ¶ The chip ignored the change: a channel is on that the driver did not switch (TRIG pin, an earlier program), or TRIGA or TRIGB is high. The driver cannot see the TRIG pins: keep them low while changing a drive mode or a side. A call returns DeviceReset ¶ A fault byte (or STATUS) read ACTIVE = 0: a supply dip reset every register (UVLO with a power-on reset). Any call can return it; the call sent nothing after the command byte, so the reset chip stays asleep with every channel off. The driver is uninitialised; call EnsureInitialized() to configure the chip again, then switch the channels you need. If it repeats, look at VM under load (inrush of the valves). If it appears with no supply dip, check SDO: a line stuck low reads as ACTIVE = 0 too. A call returns CommunicationError on a running driver ¶ A fault byte showed COMER going from 0 to 1: a write since the last clean byte had the wrong number of clocks and was ignored (p34), possibly an earlier call's. Switch every channel off first ( SetChannelsOn(0) : a switch-off is never refused, and while COMER is set it is read back), then call ApplyConfig(GetConfig()) to write the registers in doubt again (it returns ChannelsActive while a channel whose mode is in doubt could still be on) and switch the channels back on. Check SCK and CSB for glitches. The copy is not proof while COMER stays set: a switch-off is read back, but a miscounted switch-on or configuration write is seen only with Verify::ReadBack . IsMiscountDetectionDegraded() returns true in that state (no I/O): use Verify::ReadBack for the writes that must land, or restart with Deinitialize() and EnsureInitialized() , which takes ENABLE low to clear COMER. While COMER stays set, the driver keeps doubt rather than trust a write it cannot prove, by design: A channel that ApplyConfig() rewrote while another channel was on stays "of either mode", so a further ApplyConfig() change to it returns ChannelsActive , even one that changes only HOLD. SetPairMode() without Verify::ReadBack leaves its pair's mode in doubt, so the next switch-on in that pair returns Uncertain . The ways out: SetHoldCode() for a HOLD change, ConfigureChannel() with every channel off, SetPairMode(pair, mode, Verify::ReadBack) , or a restart. A switch returns Uncertain ¶ A write to STATUS failed after it may have reached the chip, and it changed this pair's mode: the chip may run either mode, and what ONCHx and ONCHy do depends on it (Tables 6 and 7). Write the mode again with SetPairMode() (or Verify::ReadBack ), or ApplyConfig() , while the pair is off. A switch-off always works: SetChannel(ch, false) or SetBridge(pair, BridgeState::HiZ) switches both channels of the pair off. A SetChannelsOn() that returns Uncertain still sent the rest of its mask; the unknown pair itself was switched off. A channel does not drive ¶ ReadStatus() : active set, on_mask has the channel, no overtemperature . ReadFaults() : OCP switches the channel off and keeps it off until it is switched off in ONCH and on again; OLF with a load fitted means the load does not reach VM (low side) or ground (high side). CDR: hit and hold not 0, Config::rref_ohm matches the resistor (IFS = 15 kΩ x 1 A / RREF), and the HIT current above the valve's pull-in current. VDR: the duty and VM give enough current. trigger_pin set: the channel follows TRIGA (even) or TRIGB (odd), not ONCH. HHF or DPM flags on a working valve ¶ HHF: the current did not reach IHIT by the end of tHIT: lengthen the HIT time or lower IHIT. DPM: no dip deeper than the threshold and longer than the debounce came between ISTART and IHIT: lower the threshold or the debounce, set ISTART just below the dip, and check that the current rises slower than 700 mA/ms above ISTART ( Drive modes ). The current is lower than set ¶ CDR regulates the peak current; the average is lower by half the ripple, which grows as the chopping frequency falls. The accuracy is ±6 % above 71 % of IFS and ±25 % from 5 % to 10 %: for small currents choose a larger RREF or HFS.

docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs kokeb-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Inside the MAX22200 ¶ Inside the MAX22200 Figure description and sources The MAX22200's function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp . Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers.
